So, what about Mordheim - City of the Damned ?
I would not recommend this game to anyone, except an hardcore suicidal masochist, it's a total waste of time, energy, and money !
As a fan of Warhammer lore and tabletop games, and of games like Valkyria Chronicles and XCOM, i thought i would enjoy Mordheim as much as possible.
Well, no. In fact, imagine a game where EVERYTHING (and when I say everyhting, I mean it) is determined by RNG. From the smallest jump to the strongest charge, every action is determined by a roll between 1 and 100, with a percentage of success.
However, in Mordheim, the RNG is biased (if you look others reviews and Mordheim general discussions threads you'll see that almost everybody agree on this point). The developpers wanted to make an ULTRA hard game... and they failed.
Mordheim is beyond hard or any difficulty you can imagine, it is designed to make you lose, whatever you do.
You can try to adapt tactics and builds, learn maps and skills, play as safe as possible, if the RNG decides that you lose your WHOLE progess (generally dozens of hours) at this battle, trust me you'll lose everything at this battle, and you'll have to start again from scratch.
Let me explain : AI's enemy units have huge buffs, even on the lowest difficulty, and the RNG works in their favor. When it says that you, as a player, have 80% hit chances (as an exemple) you'll see that you will never approach the 80% hits if you look at all your rolls. On the otherside, an AI unit with 60% hits chances will almost never miss.
These two points combined, whatever you plan to do, you are forced to lose your warband at a point (after of course tryharding it for 30+ hours).
This game is beyond difficulty and punitivity. It's just stupid and nonsensical.
Another point to not recommend this game at all is the community. There are 2 kinds of people : The new players/the kind ones that are struggling to enjoy this game, most of them leaving it after losing another warband and 50 hours of wasted time due to 0.000001% set of circumstances that happen regularly in Mordheim ; and the 5% old veterans of the game, with 1000+ hours on it, and 10 warbands max level and full purple stuff. These guys will tell you anytime you ask for a bit of help to enjoy/understand the game things like : "You suck, L2P noob and then come back." , "This game is too easy for me, you shouldn't have any problems unless you suck." and their best argue : "I have nor problem with my full min-maxed warbands so there is no problem in the game." And the worst is that they aren't trolling at all, they are dead serious...
Btw, graphics are cool, loading times are long, lore isn't respected and DLC are expensive. This game should still be an open Beta, it's full of bugs.
Don't buy it ;)

Let's get this out of the way. I dont think Sonic 4 is a bad game. I would even go as far as saying its above mediocre and mechanically satisfying to play.
I will however be approaching it from a long time Sonic the Hedgehog fan's perspective. And dont worry, im not one of those weirdos who think Sonic Adventure 2 is the best thing ever or someone  who is into creating deviantart sonic characters. For me, the pinnacle of Sonic has always been Sonic 3 & Knuckles and nothing ever since has been able to re-create that Sonic aesthetic that made him famous.
So you can imagine my entusiasm when I heard back in 2009 that a Sonic the Hedgehog 4 was being made. That name for me had the same impact as something like Half Life 3, or Star Wars Episode VII for alot of people. It was a dream come true.
It should have been warning enough for me at the time to hear that it would be split into episodes, but my fanboyism was too blinding to let that stop me from hyping it.
Long story short, I got the game and was completely underwhelmed by it. I wasnt even aware of it at the time, I was just happy to play a new 2d Sonic game. But something didnt feel right, and I left the game with a bad taste in my mouth, not really understanding why. So much so that I didnt even buy the second episode.
So, I decided to replay episode I again after all these years  to see if I can express my feelings about this game this time.
Right off the bat, the title screen. That title screen. I still remember how disappointing it was for me, so static, so empty, an empty shell of something that was once great. Everyone who played Sonic 1 as a kid remembers being greeted by Sonic waving his finger with that beautiful background behind him when they booted up the game for the first time. It's a shock now to see how much Sonic 4 misses the mark by trying to emulate that feeling, but failing completely.
We move one from that and start the game, and we are introduced once again to Green Hill Zone in disguise, yet it's uglier and more artificial this time. For some odd reason, the devs decided that the best way to re-create the genesis look was to use some of the most ugly pre-rendered graphics I have ever seen, something that makes Sonic look out of place and the level looks like it was made for some website like Newgrounds or Miniclip.
Then you hear the soundtrack. What an awful assault to the ears. Its so evidently clear they were trying to make it sound like the genesis tunes, but I have no idea how they failed this miserably. It sounds so artificial and soulless and it doesnt help that it loops so quickly, this is an insult to the outstanding tunes of the genesis games, just go on youtube and compare.
Stepping aside from that how is the gameplay? It's ok. If you havent played the genesis games, its totally servicable and there are some geniuine fun moments here and there. Stages are generally well designed and they have a way of pushing you in the right direction, even if most that is due to the homing attack that really requires no effort on the player's part other than pressing X to hit an enemy. Each act presents some sort of gimmick that provides some variety and identity to that stage, even if some gimmicks flat out make me question if the devs even knew what the hell they were doing. There is one particular puzzle in the middle of a stage that stops you right on your tracks and forces you to figure out a time based puzzle where you are forced to wait for it to reset if you fail to solve it. It's just baffling to me they would put this on a Sonic game.
The worst offender however, if you did play those genesis games, is how it handles physics. If you know anything about those early Sonic games, is that they differentiated themselves from all other platformers at the time by how they managed to insert physics based platforming, taking into consideration stuff like slopes, loops and momentum.
This game has none of that. You can plain stop in the middle of an upwards slope without falling, you can spindash in a loop that it wont make you go any faster. It astounds me that SEGA cant find good programmers to replicate what essencially was the big deal of the first Sonic game. It's simply a rollercoaster, what was once a reward for skilled players who managed to use the physics to their advantage, now speed is simply a cheap thrill that the game forces on you. While Sonic controls just fine at full speed, when you have to make him move from square one it's so awkward and sluggish, especially since they decided to go with the Modern Sonic look, making him hilariously walk like a normal person with animations that dont even match the speed he is going at.
Stages are just plain carbon copies of Sonic 1 and 2 stages, There is 4 of them, 3 acts each and then it's over. The content here is just laughable.
The bosses also manage to be worse than the old games, being rehashes of previous games and having these weird flourishes that make you wait for them to reveal their weak spots before you can hit them. The bosses from the old games worked because the agency was put in the players hands. You could destroy them in less than a minute if you had the skill to do so, bosses shouldnt force the player to wait for them to do their ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t shtick before you can have the opportunity to hit them, especially in a game that is supposed to reward speed.
Even the bonus stage sucks! It is a clone of the Sonic 1 bonus stage, but it looks atrocious, the music is also awful, and it controls like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥!
You must be tired of hearing me say "the old games did it better". And you would be right to be so, if it wasnt for one simple aspect: the game is called Sonic the Hedgehog 4. And this is my biggest problem with this game. Had this been called anything else, which it should have, I would probably give it a light recommendation and be done with it. But it has that name.
How the hell can it have that name? I will go to my grave saying that Sonic 3 & Knuckles is one of the best 2d platformers of all time, and SEGA expects me to accept this travesty of a game? How could they even do this to their fans? Is this what they really think of us? That we wil just roll on the floor and take every pile of crap that contains Green Hill Zone with gratitude?
How can a game that is simply content with re-using ideas from Sonic 1 and 2 without the actual inventiveness of said games be proclaimed the sequel to one of the best games of all time?

When Sonic 4 launched in 2010, it marked the end to a 16 year drought of new 2D console Sonic games. Promising a return to the Blue Blur’s 16 Bit Roots, SEGA, Sonic Team and Dimps had quite the legacy to live up to. Unfortunately, while the game gets the things right, there are enough glaring flaws to prevent this from being a recommendation.
After the events of Sonic 3 & Knuckles, Sonic sets off to explore new territory alone, meaning no Tails or Knuckles, just like Sonic 1 on the Genesis. However, Dr. Ivo “Eggman” Robotnik survived his last encounter with Sonic and decides to take some of his previous creations, slightly revise them, and eliminate Sonic once and for all as the first part of his new grandiose plan.
The gameplay is tried and true for the Blue Hedgehog, you collect rings, dodge spikes, attack badnicks to free animal critters trapped inside while navigating the stage as quickly as you can. If you collect enough rings, you have the chance to get a Chaos Emerald at the end of each Act. Collect all 7, and you’ll become the invincible Super Sonic, who has access to a double jump, and can go even faster than Sonic normally can. After a few Acts of a Zone, you are presented with a boss battle, featuring the aforementioned Doctor, always sporting a new contraption to try and kill Sonic.
As fans of Sonic’s Handheld outings know, Dimps has plenty of experience making 2D Sonic games. It may come as a surprise then that Dimps efforts just fall short. On a checklist, Sonic 4 Episode 1 hits most of the things they tried to do, incorporate elements from the old games, add in the homing attack, and appeal to Genesis’ fans nostalgia. The issue with that is that they didn’t do much else. The physics feel completely off from the Genesis games, and there is an issue with momentum. Sonic can be running up a slope, and right when he reaches the top, if he doesn’t have enough speed, he just stops. Sonic is now standing completely horizontal, creating a 90 degree angle with the terrain he was just running up.
The level design also leaves something to be desired. Taking inspiration from Sonic 1 and 2, the 4 main levels are heavily inspired by Green Hill, Casino Night, Labyrinth Zone, and Metropolis Zone, with signature elements from each zone often being recycled. While these nods are nice, they are done far too often to simply be paying homage. This feeling is reinforced by the same badniks occupying the levels as the originals, and the boss fights often being exactly the same, but with a small change instead. The game does sport some original ideas in zones, but these ideas come across as being gimmicks instead of good level design.
If you were hoping the special stages were spared, I regret to inform you that they weren’t. Instead of using Sonic 2’s halfpipe that many a Sonic game has used, Sonic 4 Episode 1 goes back to the original special stage, but they only proceeded to make it more frustrating by removing your control of Sonic. Before, you navigated Sonic around the stage, now you rotate the stage around Sonic. In addition to this frustrating change, there is now a timer on the special stage, and you need to reach the Chaos Emerald before you run out of time. The inclusion of time boosting items in the stage helps, but the equivalent of applying a bandage to a gunshot wound.
Not even the soundtrack was spared in this release. Typically, a Sonic game may be terrible, but still have an outstanding soundtrack, but I personally found it lackluster compared to previous Sonic soundtracks. The same can be said for the graphics of the game. While by no means bad, they just aren’t that good either. Sadly, the game looks better in screenshots than in motion.
Overall, Sonic 4 Episode 1 is a mixed bag. Many mistakes were made along the way, one of the biggest being drawing too much from the classics. The lack of a proper physics engine, and the momentum being off takes away enjoyment from the levels, and the attached gimmicks do more harm than good. I wish I could recommend this game, I wish Steam gave me the option to mark the game as Mixed instead of Recommend or Don’t Recommend, but there are so many glaring flaws that I can’t recommend it. If you are a Sonic Fan, then you should pick up the game on sale at some point, because you’ll probably still have some fun with the game. If you aren’t, then you shouldn’t consider buying this game for any more than 5 dollars.

Never before has a game made me so excited to find a marble.
Jokes aside, this game is truly spectacular, brought me to tears on multiple occasions.
Got it on sale during the 2017 Summer Sale, but felt like I UNDERPAID. So I went to the bandcamp page for the soundtrack (which is pay-what-you-want), and paid $30 for it to make up for it.

It's been days since I finished this game and the story, characters, and especially the ending are still fresh in my head. The comparisons to To the Moon are 100% justified. Every character feels three-dimensional, every location feels lived-in. The story deals with some dark and heavy topics, such as losing a family member, racism, dementia/Alzheimer's, etc, but it's all handled very well without feeling like it's being smashed over your head. There were at least four separate times in the story where I actually teared up.
But most importantly, it's a game about being friendly. The whole point is to be kind and helpful to everyone you know, and in return, you'll make friends who want to be kind and helpful for you. It just feels good to play a game with that kind of message.
Ultimately, if you're a fan of story heavy games, and if you're okay with dealing with some prickly, mature topics, then by all means buy this game and support the creator and her crew. She definitely deserves all the praise she's been given for this.

I just can't recommend this game, no matter how much I'd like to do so.
- Sonic is simply too slow. Replace him with any other character and you'll be playing just another platformer. Also, the controls are not very responsive and oftentimes you'll fall just because Sonic takes time to jump after you give the command. And that homing attack... so, so inaccurate.
- The level design is (mostly) awfully poor and comes down to 2 frustrations -
1. Not knowing where you're supposed to go next;
2. Losing a life due to an unexpected fall since you can't tell the background objects from the "real" ones.
- There are 4 worlds (and one ultimate boss level):
The first world is that generic introductory one all platformers have. It's as generic as it can get.
The second one is all colors, and trial and error in terms of where you're supposed to go.
The third one would fit any other platformer well; not Sonic, though, as there are too many obstales/stops, hence you can't dash/run for more than 2-3 seconds.
The last one... is actually a decent world with some nice level of challenge and Sonic elements. However, it's far too little to make up for the previous ones.
- The Eggman encounters are... strange at best. The first and second encounter are too easy, the third one is ridiculously difficult (compared to the previous two), while the fourth one is a matter of timely jumps. And then, you meet him one last time where you get to see him in all previous "forms" plus an ultimate one... which is, again, too easy.
- I don't think graphics make a game, but in this case, they really do harm. They just add up to the feeling you're playing a rushed, unpolished game.
- The music is cool. It really is. Yay!
Will give Episode 2 a try as well. I like Sonic and I hate what they did to him. Hopefully, Sonic Mania will bring some of Sonic's glory back, as he deserves it.

Sonic the hedgehog 4 Episode 1 is a 2d platformer developed by Sonic Team and released Jan 19, 2012. Sonic the hedgehog 4 episode 1 was supposed to be the successor to the generally beloved Sonic the Hedgehog 3 and knuckles.
There's no story really. Some people will be very pleased to hear there's no dialogue, you don't hear Eggman or Sonic speak, you don't see any characters other then Sonic. It's just Sonic Chasing down Eggman who's back to his old tricks, turning the woodland creatures into robots.
Actually it's borderline "LITERALLY" back to his OLD tricks, because we're back in green Hills as the first 3 levels, then boss... and the boss is exactly the same as the first sonic boss with the wrecking ball and two platforms, on my nolstalgia, oh my heart! <3
The controls are beautifuly simple, movement using directional keys or controller directional pad, and then pressing a button to jump, or holding down and pressing  a button to spin dash, or pressing down while moving to go into ball form.
The change in this rendition is the physics have been updated or wrecked... depending on whom you ask. I didn't care and didn't notice anything. But I've never been very "good" at sonic games. So this is coming from someone who just barely beats the game but rarely gets the complete ending by getting all the chaos emeralds.

The biggest change for me was the new homing attack feature. I feel like it's useful, but often times too slow paced for sonic
. But while a bit slow I thought it was better then relying on my pin-point-jumping-skills, because those died when I stopped playing platformers every single day.
Regarding the levels and content of Sonic the hedgehog 4 Episode 1: There are 5 worlds each with 3 levels, then a boss level. After completing a "score level" you can replay it in time attack mode, and then compare times with your friends... ....is what I'd say if any of my friends had scores
.
To put it simply: Sonic the hedgehog 4 Episode 1 was EXACTLY what I was expecting going into it. I wasn't remotely disappointed.
However, I would say that any of the classic SEGA Sonic Games (1, 2, 3, and knuckles) is better then this one. Sonic the hedgehog 4 Episode 1 wasn't as bad as many of the 3d games released for the PS2, and gamecube, and certainly could have been worse (you want to complain about bad physics? Go look at Sonic 06.)
Honestly at this point who knows what sonic fan's even want, I doubt they themselves know what they want. Some may agree with me, some might right nasty messages on my wall, regardless I like Sonic the hedgehog 4 Episode 1, See you in Episode 2.

I've put a bit of time into this game now.
It has one of the best combat systems I've had the pleasure to play, once you get used to the major differences it has with other games. Everything For Honor wanted to be, Absolver is, at least in terms of combat, and Absolver has massively greater customization. Anyone saying combat slowly devolves into a certain optimal strategy simply hasn't played enough; while there are balance issues, the developers have demonstrated a willingness to address them in a decent manner, and none of them are insurmountable. Once you pass a certain learning curve, what initially seemed oppressive becomes free kills (for most, this is spammed fast attacks mixed with guard breaks, which you have to understand the defense system to deal with).
That being said, there is a lack of content; even with the upcoming 3v3 (and private 1v1) mode that will be released in the next few weeks, PvE has about 6 hours if you take your time, and outside of that there's 1v1s, with no ranked system yet. Progression comes in the form of lootboxes (no microtransactions, which is obviously a good thing), and a "prestige" system that gives you ever-better triangles next to your name.
Still, the developers have indicated that every part of the game will see expansion, from movesets to overworld zones, and most of the glaring issues have been resolved. This game is worth buying now, and will only get better.
If you like PvP, this is a solid choice.

Rakuen is one of those rare games that I would classify more as an experience than a game.
I have to admit that it has one of the most heart-wrenching story/collection of stories I've ever played in a video game. It relentlessly tells the story of a child in the hospital dealing with a crippling illness and copes with it by entering an imaginary world with this mother. With this imaginary world and the real world connected through the book Rakuen, this boy goes on adventures to try to fulfill a wish, while helping those around him in the process.
The storytelling of this game is absolutely top-notch and with a composer and singer like Laura Shigihara (Plants vs. Zombies, To The Moon) creating the music to this spectacle, it makes for a phenomenal experience. Shigihara's atmospheric composition ties everything together so perfectly that it makes for an incredible gaming experience.
I wouldn't call it a perfect game. I did feel there were segments of the game where the story sort of dragged itself out while other parts felt way too short compared to other developed parts of the game. There was also one certain part of the story I found confusing and couldn't figure out how it tied together, but it could have been something missed in the story.
However, my criticisms of this game were extremely limited because this was such a compelling gaming experience that if I did notice any flaws, they were completely forgotten due to how engrossing the story was.
I cannot recommend this game highly enough, especially if you loved a game like To The Moon. The one thing I would warn going into this game is it is not for the faint of heart. This game is nearly relentless with how hard it hits with its melancholic storytelling. I am convinced if you do not cry at least once during this game, you do not have a soul. I can't count on one hand how many times this game made me tear up. That is just how well this game was executed in its narrative.

This was a game that had two levels, the Surface Layer and the Deeper Meaning. Using RPG-Maker as the structure, it provided some lighthearted (and sometimes darker) music to set the mood as you did various miniquests, tasks, and solved puzzles over a 6-8 hour story. The story of a boy in a hospital, going on adventures to help people in the Real World by stepping into their memories and dreams and fixing various aspects of them. This fantasy world reflects and affects the Real World, such that similarly named people, objects, and details exist in both (water a plant in the real world, and it goes from sapling to beanstalk in the fantasy, for instance). Seems pretty simple...
...But then there's the Deeper Meaning. Via newspaper clippings, inferred meaning, and various details you have put together for yourself from clues and comments in-game, everyone and everything has something a bit more in-depth than what's on the surface. Every time I got a bit annoyed at some fetch quest or RPG trope, I'd see a hint of something more meaningful beneath it, and follow that thread until I reached the end. Each of these Deeper Meanings made me mist up a bit, and eventually culminated in a wonderful combination of story, music, and character that choked me up but good.
I could go on about plot or graphics or sound or anything else, but really I'm recmmending this game because of those Deeper Meanings. While I'm sure I could compare it to To The Moon (or Bird Story), in the end this is a game that stands alone. It has a strong soundtrack, original music and vocals, excellent game mechanics, and clever writing that can be both touching and humorous. I'd highly recommend this to anyone who can put aside a few hours and get to know a few wonderful people, in a hospital, and go on a magical adventure. It may not have combat or fighting, but I still felt something while I was playing it...and that's wonderful from such a simple and yet well-made game.

Disclaimer: I don't know the boardgame, in fact, I'm not even a big fan of any of Games Workshops realms.
Now with 45 hours put into the game, I finally feel that I can write about it. I have been waiting quite some time for a decent sale to get this game, being ever excited about it, despite the negative meh-cloud around it. I have read many thing about it as well and just couldn't find an aspect that could serve as a base for all the shouting. But anyways, I wanted to see for myself.
First of all, let's get clear on a couple of things here: If you do the tutorial, read the descriptions, basically if you catch up with Mordheim's story - like I had to - you will realize that this city was never ment to provide you a cloudless, happy-go-lucky lifestyle. In fact it was ment to end you. To drop you in a bubbling bowl of gooey green slime where you will most probably die a slow, slow painfull death. Sorry. I had to take you there. Among the life threatening, unforgiving conditions you will actually get the slightest chance at surviving, now that's where you start with your warband. Knowing now what I'm talking about I strongly believe that the majority of negative reviews of this wonderfull war-management game are the result of a mere misunderstanding. You don't even get to select a difficulty level, this game was ment to be harsh on you! Because we are talking a "random number generator" system, you will have a pretttty high number of chances at failing, equal to the sides of the dice you're rolling. Pls don't let me get into maths (I couldn't anyway), but the gist is: you will never be able to measure up and calculate your steps ahead precisely. And that's that! You either play by these rules, or you can just as well drop this game, it's simply not for your liking.
The game's most criticized aspect, the rng is partially what gives you all the excitement in the city of the damned. It's just thrilling to get deployed onto the yet unknown maps with most of the outcomes an obscurity as well. You'll try to do your best and prepare for the worst you know (ha ha, how sweet of you!).  Meanwhile, the game is heavy on the management side too. You don't just skirmish around a map, you are also obliged to fulfill a certain mysterious lord with shipments of green gems that - oh by the way - can hurt you while picking them up. This is the main reason you stick around an awful city giving you the creeps: it's your job to collect these stones and sell them for currency that you can actually use to manage and keep up your warband, while also paying their medical insurance, sick leaves, overtime, studies, a 546 channel cabel package with online streaming and probably pension too, dammit!
The random missions to get your resources could easily get dull after some time, but here comes the storyline! Every now and then, a new story mission will be asked of you. It's mostly up to you when you fulfill them, but you won't advance untill you don't deal with them one by one. I have found the story missions I have faced so far truly intiguing and exciting.
So that's what we have here:
- Asskicking and demanding turn-based combat with heavy management features when not fighting -
I like the aspect of the different races, their varying outfits, the character customizations (god I hate to lose those chaps!), the equipment proficiencies, they all spice up the game.
One negative aspect I could point out though: a soprano in the background... I wish there was more time put into the music of the whole game. it only gets boring first, but after some time the soprano's terrible screaming gets to your nerves (her voice actually cracks at one time, or doesn't it??) I'm playing with the music muted now.
All in all, I can full-heartedly recommend this game for anyone who doesn't mind a perma death challange with rng in it.

My review of Mordheim: City of the Damned
I believe a rating system of 1-5 would be better than the binary yes/no Steam uses.  Overall I would rate this game somwhere near 2.5.  Since there is not, I would have to not recommend this game.
The pros and cons:
Pros:
Immersive world
Good music
Warhammer
Game-to-game advancement
Cons:
Based mostly on randomness
Shallow gameplay
Poor balance
To summarize, Mordheim is a squad-based game in which you complete missions to varying degrees of success in order to loot the remains of the city of Mordheim.  The game feels fairly tabletop-ish with most mechanics based on measures and die-rolls.  There is an advancement and permanent-ish injury system which leads to unique gameplay situations.  Overall I found all this as appealing, particularly considering this is set in the Warhammer universe.  Going game-to-game and playing for not just the moment but the next several as well in a post-apocalyptic warhammer world.
Why I cannot recommend this game, however, is disappointing.  There are 6 factions available right now including DLC.  Considering the majority of missions revolve around one side retreating, these factions are not close to balanced.  The game has a definite hierarchy of concerning the difficulty of factions.  At the top, the easiest and therefore toughest factions are the Sisters of Sigmar and the Undead.  Slow but physically dominant factions.  In a rough order following those 2 are the Skaven, Human Mercenaries, Witch Hunters, and Cult of the Possessed.  Worse now, is that there are minimal differences between each of them as the game progress.
All factions consist of 1 leader, 3 hero options, 1 prestige class, and 2 henchmen.  All classes have their own attributes, proficiences (which dictate gear), spells, and somewhat different skills.  Skills are mostly shared across all classes and are based on statistics.  Attributes are capped based on class but not that significantly.  Spells are the most significant difference between classes as either you have access to Divine or Arcane or neither.  The combination of these 4 facets differentiate classes.  This means that through advancement most classes can match others.  I find this rather undesirable as a caster can be as proficient physically as most melee classes.  This lends itself to the Sisters and Cult being rather better in the longer-game.  I have the Cult lower mostly because they start as the whipping boys that you are glad to see as your opponent early in campaigns.  Not to mention the fact that the devs somehow thought that giving the Sisters a normal-sized prestige class was somehow balanced.
I bought the game on significant sale which made it mostly worth.  Hopefully further content will be released which expands upon variety.  I wouldn't spend more than $20 on it as it currently stands.  I feel most people looking for a challenge will end up at the same point I am at.  The game is either too easy or unskillfully difficult which leads to boredom.

I honestly can't believe this game is free. It was a pleasure to play and the art, writing, and gameplay are all done to a very high standard, so if you're wondering whether to check it out - do it!
The character routes are all quite different from each other and took longer to complete than I was expecting; it's easy to see that a lot of effort has gone into every aspect of the game. The plot is well thought out and the love interests all have a distinctive design and personality - I especially liked the
I was also relieved to discover that they all lack that sort of overly rude or demeaning attitude that a lot of otome games seem to think manly men need in order to be attractive, and that their conflict came across clearly without resorting to blaming or insulting the protagonist. Sad that this seperates the game from many others in this day and age but there you go. If I had to put it into words, I'd say that the game as a whole was a very positive experience; you don't find yourself irritated or emotionally drained after playing - not too much anyway.
I found some of the character development particularly interesting, although (and I'm kind of nitpicking here) sometimes I felt it could have gone a bit deeper or focused on the dynamic of the relationship a little more. For example, sometimes it felt as if there was external conflict and then suddenly - they're in love!
The plot is very politically dramatic, if that makes sense, and less so when it comes to the relationships.
The art is very unique and beautiful, I especially love the eyes - they made the MC look fantastically cold and shrewd sometimes - I lived for her evil glare. On that note it was very fun seeing things from her perspective, she is one of the most interesting characters in the game. It would have been nice to see more recognition from the other characters regarding her
, as I think it's only briefly mentionned on the one route and I felt that really could have added to her developement or the ANGST.
Overall though I made it through every route very easily and it was a joy to play - I can't wait to see what Dicesuki does next.

TD;LR:  As a game, Resident Evil 4 is cult classic and a very rewarding survival/horror experience that needs very little explanation.  As a port and “upgrade” to the original experience, the game does mostly right and a few wrongs, but overall it is a better game because of it.  Updated graphics, a 60 FPS experience, and some other, more minor details have brought this game up to modern standards from its PS2 days.
I don’t consider myself a fan of the survival/horror genre, especially of newer titles which, to me at least, rely on appalling amounts of gore, cheap jump-scares, and cliché gameplay mechanics.  This game was an exception, being the only survival/horror I had played for a time.
Resident Evil 4 is (broken record warning) a survival/horror game placing you in the shoes of Leon Kennedy, a survivor of Raccoon City, who has been tasked with finding the president’s daughter.  The game emphasizes resource and hit management as ammo and health items are uncommon and rewards exploration which can result in finding more of these items and then some.
The game starts you off with some basic items, a handgun, some ammo, and a med kit, and immediately places you in the middle of the action.  Combat must be done quickly and precisely as allowing yourself to be overwhelmed is a quick way to end the game and wasting all your ammo will have you resorting to the knife which is not an easy experience.  Items like weapons and your inventory are upgradable, so you can make your weapons more powerful and your inventory larger.  The game does a nice balance between regular combat and boss fights, where fighting common enemies is where you should conserve ammo and bosses allow you to be more generous in ammo usage.  The story is told in three acts, taking place in three
expansive levels with hidden clues, items, and other treasures.
As a game, it does survival/horror very well.  The mechanics like limited ammo and massive damage from enemies create a very real fear of death in the game whether you are facing a horde of Ganados or a boss like Salazar.  This fear is what makes Resident Evil 4 so great, in my opinion.  I cannot tell you how many times I had to put down the controller and take a breather because I had come within inches of having to restart the level.  There are not many games that can do that and do it well.
As a port, this game is done well compared to other ports PCs have gotten in the past.  It actually works, for one (No, I am not referring to a specific port here…I don’t know what you are talking about), and provides a few extra options you would expect from a regular PC game.  Graphics options are limited, putting low-end machines at a disadvantage, and the graphics are not as upgraded as you might expect, though they have been cleaned up.  I recommend a controller while playing this game as the keyboard-mouse controls are a bit unusual and a controller provides a much better experience for this game.  To top it off, the game runs at 60 FPS, but there are other framerate options if you have a weaker machine.
Resident Evil 4 does well in both respects and still provides great gameplay.  Veteran players will find the game to be as enjoyable now as it was back in the PS2 days, and newcomers can expect a unique survival/horror experience.  Until next time, GG and Good Hunting.

You will spend a lot of time setting and resetting the controls when starting out before you finally realize this game has about 2 or 3 more buttons than it even needs.  For example, there's an Interact button, but when you're in menus, the Melee Attack button is used as Confirm.  It takes a couple runthroughs of setting the buttons before you start noticing little weird things like this that make it really hard to find a comfortable control scheme.  There's so many buttons that you're going to have to compromise and put certain things on shoulder buttons that you really don't want up there.
Game designers usually strive for less buttons because making a huge list of buttons with exactly one function makes the player have to constantly stop and try to remember what does what.  The popular solution most games have used is give buttons multiple functions based on context.
So often you come across an object in this game and you have to go "wait, do I push up or down? Do I push interact? Or do I bonk it with my sword?"  And you have to make these decisions in dangerous environments with traps and enemies.  Even navigating menus is way more complicated than it should be.
This game is playable if you really put in the work to find a good control scheme, and then do some rote memorization.  But, this is just a 2d RPG platformer, there's no reason why the controls need to be so complex.
I think if the devs sit down and honestly try to simplify the controls and make it more intuitive for a wide audience of players, they'd have a real classic on their hands.  This game is fantastic otherwise, but I just can't imagine it becoming very popular with these confusing controls.

Vagante is one of the best 4-player, shared-screen, cooperative, roguelike, semi-permadeath dungeon-crawling platformers I ever played.  It's not quite as challenging or clever as Rogue Legacy, but Vagante supports multiple players, so it has that as a major advantage.  It's fast-paced, scary at times, and has a lot of explorable environments (it's a roguelike, duh, it has infinite environments).  It provides you with 4 seemingly unisex character classes, a level-up system, equipment, standard potions and other healing items, and magic spells learned mostly from spellbooks.  Combat is difficult but simple enough for new players to jump right in.  Players cannot hot-join or join in the middle of dungeon levels, but there are break zones or lobby areas to chill, let players join, and prepare for the next level.
Overall, Vagante is well worth its initial price of $14.99, even if you only play alone, because it provides a fairly well polished experience that's simply not common in the roguelike genre.  It's great for multiple players, as well, and I bought the game for that purpose.  I'm completely satisfied even though the game is in Early Access.

Life of a Wizard is pretty short, about 1-2 hours per playthrough, but the world and plotlines are interesting and the game has solid replay value. Gameplay consists of reading short passages about events and choosing how you act and react to them as the game unfolds, taking the form of an interactive choose-your-own-adventure story. You create your own wizard character and live out his or her life from childhood until retirement. Character progression is very D&D-esque and every individual choice, of which there are many, can significantly alter how the rest of your game plays out. It's a simple but creative concept and I think that this game does it well. If you have a few bucks in your Steam wallet and want a light but engaging fantasy rpg experience, consider trying out Life of a Wizard.

Sonic the Hedgehog 4 - Episode I is far from perfect. It's way too short, it's too easy, it doesn't look that great (especially compared to Episode II), the whole game reeks of unoriginality, and the physics can be ridiculous at times (though to be honest I only noticed that significantly when I was TRYING to exploit it). However I still found the game to be fairly fun, because it still gets most of the basic core gameplay of Sonic down right. It controls quite well, the level design is interesting and I never encountered any glitches. There is basically nothing spectacular about it, you should save your money for Episode II or Generations if you have to pick, but if you're a big Sonic fan the gameplay is sound enough to maybe warrant a look at. It's far from the messes that some other modern Sonic games have been, but it does not even remotely live up to being the sequel of the three (or three and a half?) Genesis installments. I think I would recommend every other 2D Sonic game on Steam before it, but it's still a fun distraction, though nothing more than that.

This game is an obvious recommendation to those that like the web-comic “Sandra and Woo”, but I will also recommend it to those that enjoy classic style point and click adventure games with likeable characters.
There’s little doubt in my mind, that you will find enjoyment in the game if you have already fallen in love with the main characters of the comic, but knowledge of the comic is not required to enjoy the game, if you are up for a cute and silly adventure game with a group of likeable preteens.
Let us begin with the negatives, as I like getting those out of the way first.
Some of the animations are a bit stiff, didn’t really bother me much, since I feel the most important thing in the adventure game is the dialogue, and I enjoy playing some adventure games from the 2000s. (And not because of nostalgia. :P I actually only got properly into adventure games a few years ago.)
The minigames. The minigames are skippable, so again not a big negative, but yeah, a lot of them were more on the annoying side for me breaking away from the humor and fun of the main game. You might experience them more as a fun variation in gameplay, depends on taste.
Larisa’s face looked a bit creepy when she stood facing the camera directly. I don’t know if it was just a poor choice of design for her face, or if it was an intention to give her a “crazy eyes”/ “crazy look”. The thing is, Larisa doesn’t look crazy in the comics. Her actions, and the things she says is often absolutely crazy, but she doesn’t look crazy at a glance. I feel that she does in this game… Then again, that might just be me.
Last negatives are only relevant to the webcomic fans:
Some of the best side characters are missing. I admit, this negative is a bit more a personal preference, but it is especially annoying since my least favorite side-character Landon has a sizeable role in the story. I’d much rather have seen Cloud’s mom and sister or… Well really anyone other than Landon. :P The guy is dull compared to the rest of the cast...
The game captures the world of the comics very well, and Sandra and Woo fits very well into a point and click adventure game, even before they get sucked into the “game world”. Since the “real world” in the comic already operates under a different set of rules from our own, natural laws and the fourth wall can be broken for the sake of comedy. Given the protagonists and the world, some of the sillier solutions in this kind of game makes sense, since you are thinking “If I was an imaginative child, how would I solve this?”
The game is fully voiced which is nice, though there are sometimes some words that don’t match the subtitles 1:1, but that kind of stuff occurs in a lot of games. Since I didn’t notice any points in the game where what was said and what was written had opposite meaning, then I don’t see any issue. Giving voices to characters from a silent medium is always a challenge. On the one hand fans might be excited to finally hear the characters they love… On the other hand, the voices can’t possibly fit what everyone assumed they sounded like when they read the comic. In my case, I think the voices fit, especially the boys and Sandra. I was surprised that Larisa had an accent, I mean I knew her parents were Russian, but I just assumed she was so young when she came to the country, and given she hung out with kids without accents that she would have grown out of it? By no means an up or a down, and I probably will continue to picture her without one. Just shows how difficult it can be to match people’s expectations, when you go from different medias.
The characters are likeable, adorable, and fun. From Cloud trying to be a hero and save his girl, to Larisa being bored whenever she can’t cause chaos, to Woo being his mix of lazy and mischievous, to Sandra being sweet and cute and still very much proactive when she has the opportunity. Okay I don’t like Landon, but he is very much faithful to his portrayal in the comics… I just hope that if they make a new adventure game that Larisa and Landon will have broken up in the comics as he has outstayed his comedic potential a long time ago. :P The jokes with him both in this game and in the comics are pretty much just going on repeat… The personalities of the characters are very much present in the game, and leads to some funny dialogue. Like trying to use handcuffs on Cloud when playing as Larisa (which doesn’t do anything else), she mentions that Sandra would probably kill her. And since the dialogue is the most important thing for me in an adventure game, it is nice to say it fits very well.
I’ll just leave a link to the webcomic here in the end, in case any one wants to check that out too. 😊

I like this game for two reasons: I'm a fan of the Sandra and Woo webcomic, and the writing here does reflect the tone and "logic" of the webcomics, which is a huge plus for me; I am also a huge fan of puzzle games, and this game provided some very challenging puzzles which is also another plus for me.
However, I find the use of 3D wholly unnecessary, especially when the animations are all very painstakingly slow that every reaction feels like slogging through mud. For reference, the 2000 game Escape from Monkey Island, the first 3D game in the Monkey Island series, has much better 3D animation quality in terms of smoothness, not to mention the 3D models look a lot better as well. The voice acting is abysmal, especially when the voice actors don't even seem to know what tone to take on for their lines. At some points, the difference in Cloud's tone is very obvious, even the voice is not consistent, almost sounding like two different persons are his voice actors. There are also inconsistencies between the voice acting and the subtitles, and you should get the grammar of the game checked by a professional since the message about bonus moves during the mini games is just grammatically wrong, and there was an instance where "Sixth" became "
" in the game. My advice to the developer would be to ditch the 3D which provides no positive value whatsoever to the user experience; in fact, 2D is more flexible and you can go nuts with it. Take a look at the mobile games White Island and Beyond The Bounds, both by VisualShower Corp; they're both fully 2D, and the visual novel style of making characters pop up when talking also engages the audience better with facial expressions. Speaking of which, sometimes when the characters have speech bubbles for choices, their avatar beside the speech bubble does not match their in-game appearance, most obviously due to their clothing.
In conclusion, I would like to say that I enjoyed the game, but at the same time I am also very frustrated by the game's painful animations. The developer should use 2D instead of 3D since the 3D does not improve user experience and instead takes away from user experience, and voice acting direction should be provided, otherwise remove voice acting for background characters.

Hello there Woo fans and everyone who might become one,
usually I dont write reviews since I always seem to have trouble finding the right words, but this time Ill make an exception. Sandra and Woo in the Cursed Adventure is a point and click adventure with many interesting puzzles and lovable characters.
The plot is simple. You play as Sandra, waking up at night because you forgot to create your costume for a school theater rehearsal. After finishing it and going back to sleep, your computer activates and shoots some laser beams that sucked in everything they hit. Even Sandra and her raccoon Woo. Basically Sandra gets sucked into a videogame.
From that point on the characters you play with change several times while you progress through the game. You control Woo in the gameworld to find and rescue Sandra who has been captured by some guards of a nearby castle. And since It doesnt take long until Sandras friends (Larisa and Cloud) notice shes missing they try to find and of course get her out of the gameworld.
The game switches between gameworld where you have to progress with Sandra and Woo and the realworld where you have to progress with Larisa and Cloud to find clues on how to get Sandra out of the gameworld.
All Characters used in the game have origins in the web-comic "Sandra and Woo" by Powree and Oliver Knörzer. In my opinion the game does a really good job in reflecting the characters of the comic. Some surroundings looks familiar, but after crosschecking the comic I couldnt really find many similarities between the places in the comic or the game. Which of course is not a bad thing, since for instance Sandras room doesnt really have a set appearance but changes more often.
I really like the main menu of the game. When you start the game you see a tree surrounded with some stuff and two flags. the Flag of Germany and the Flag of the United Kingdom. Everyone should get that this screen is supposed to be a language selection. But compared to other games that only have a static list to choose the language from you get it presented in a creative way. The real Main menu is pretty much standard for a game like this. Same screen. I had some problems finding the save/load button. But tooltips helped.
The different places in the game are well designed and with one exception they all look realistic. The exception can be found on the screenshots of the game above (Of course only if you are on the games shop site). When you look at the image with the limonade stand you may notice that the appearance of the driveway and the bushes next to it does not really work (The grass under the bushes looks like its about 50cm under the driveway. But thats the only thing I noticed regarding that matter.
The characters animations look fine. They move like people are supposed to move and I really liked the climbing animation near the end of the game. But sadly the characters animations and the backgrounds artwork doesnt really fit together. You can see that the characters walk on the backgrounds and are not really part of it. I found some places where the characters are supposed to be behind something but are in front of it which made it look unrealistic. Also on some rooms the angle of the character standing up didnt match the angle of the walls on the perspective you can see.
I mean it doesnt really hurt the gameplay but are still some minor things you cannot unsee.
I read in some other reviews that the sounds of some things are not realistic enough, or just strange. I can agree with that but personally I had no problems with it. The sounds of the different items or things you can interact with were fitting and enhanced my games experience (Except for the kissing sound that was... strange).
Since I am German I started the game with German voices first, but after the Tutorial I decided to restart the game and play it on English. The German Voices sounded like German words with English like pronunciations. I cannot really describe it, but personally i preferred the English ones.
The English voices were good. Especially the voice actor of Larisa did a very good job in my opinion. The overall audio quality was ok. Not the best but enough for this type of game.
What I found really really frustrating were some audio errors or bugs related to sound I encountered. Especially near the end of the game when talking to Spuknit you could see him talking but neither got any sound nor subtitles. This really frustrated me since that took a lot from the ending. It was just okay somethings happening... "Someone is talking.", "No idea what hes talking about.", "Okay now I am here and I have to do this to finish.", "Aha yeah whatever."
Progressing through the game really reminded me of Deadalics Deponia Series. You run around the level, hammer your spacebar to try to find the piece you are missing to continue, but you just dont find it. These moments can be very annoying but thats what I like about point and click adventures. And this is no criticism at all. This is exactly how games of that kind should be.
Unlike the Deponia games the item combinations made sense to me. I didnt have to think super abstract to figure out what to combine and since the number of items you could have is overseeable you also had no problem just trying some combinations.
I must admit that I needed the Walkthrough 3 times. But only one time because I was really stuck and didnt know how to progress. The other two times I already had the solution but did not see on what to click to trigger the event to progress. I think its really nice that the Guide comes with the game as a free additional download. On other games you may end up watching a video for the solution which may also spoil you other parts of the game you yet have to discover. With the guide I just knew on which page I had to search for and it didnt take spoil me at all.
The minigames were doable but still challenging. You had the option to skip them if necessary but it was fine.
Also Standard for Point and Click adventures, left click to interact, right click to look at, and mouse wheel to open inventory. Thats all you need and its all you want.
Sadly the game did well on wasting my time. There were strange location changes of the characters when trying to talk to someone or interact with something. (like running around the Cow to talk to it, even if already next to it), Or Cloud chasing Larisa for 10 Seconds before the conversation started.
I wish room-changes were faster (Animation skip started after 3 Seconds). I mean its Cool to see the Characters moving, but maybe a "double click fast-travel option" would be useful. Also it would be nice to get instant feedback on not-working combinations. Instead of the character moving there to just tell me it wont work.
Also when I dont have any more topics to talk about with a Specific person. It would just be enough to say "I dont have anything left to say" or something like that. A "Hi" followed by "Bye" doesst make any sense.
There is space for optimization.
Sadly I am about to reach the size limit of a review. So Ill just add my conclusion. I enjoyed the game. And If you are fan of the web-comic you might as well. The story and the characters are good. Animation and Sound as well as Gameplay need more work. Especially the sound at the end not working was really annoying. (Hope that one gets fixed)
So If you are fan of the comic and like point and click adventures the game is for you. Otherwise you might not like it. This game is no Day of the Tentacle and by Far no Deponia. But still it Took me about 9 hours to finish. And I had fun while doing so.
Oh and Kids: Sitting in A bathtub full of ice wont give you a cold and could otherwise cause severe damages. So dont try this at home.

When you want to get away from reality, what is better than to get sucked into your favorite video game. While books are close to that level, video games easily can with the interactivity. So it is not rare for someone to wish they were actually apart of another world rather than the one they are apart of. But what if you were sucked in involuntarily?
This is what exactly happens to Sandra and Woo on the fateful day of the last rehearsal for a school play. Sandra wakes up from a nightmare, depending on selecting a tutorial or not this varies in length, with her naked on stage she is understandably nervous. As Sandra is playing the Swan, and didn’t make costume till the last second, you help her gather all of the clothing items before her father comes in to scold her about not being in bed. Strangely throwing herself back into bed still in her costume moments before she gets sucked into her computer and thus a fantasy video game in the same era of the play. Luckily they get a chance at having an adventure.
This leaves Sandra’s friends Larisa, Cloud, and Landon to wonder what happened to Sandra and why she was absent from school. With Larisa and Cloud originally finding Sandra missing, and most of her room, they enlist Landon to help with the technical aspects after finding out about the game. Trying to figure out how to get her out by using something from the real world, with the ultimate solution being smart and honestly not what I would've thought of.
On this note, I do think some things could've been worked on for the models and some of the sound effects. The character models do look like they belong in that world for sure, but the animations do need to be worked on as I often found them needing to look straight on before talking. The voice acting does depend between characters, but luckily the main characters do have solid people behind them. Though honestly, there is an actual swan that shows up that I thought did a great job in playing a ditsy princess that thinks they lost their prince...even though it is a dark timeline for her. There are two sound effects I did not exactly like. One of them did not make sense in context, and this is towards a quest in finding a bell for a jester. By the sound effect it sounds like a bell you would ring to get a cashier’s attention, even the indention looks like it, but in reality it is a bell you would put on a costume. And lastly, the kissing sound effect which turns a sweet scene off with how it echoes and how high pitched it is.
I really liked this back and forth between sceneries and characters. Both sides of the story contrast well together, and even flipping the script. While sure Sandra and Woo is literally in a fantasy video game they are doing those quests you will often get such as fetching an item from a hidden place. So when it switches back to Larisa and Cloud, they are trying to find solutions that end up exiting and the events that up the stakes happen here before they become visible to Sandra and Woo. They all also have their own different puzzles (excluding one) they need to solve and they do go about solving it their own way and different values. While Cloud refuses to look through someone’s mail and damage property, Larisa barely cares. And a little thing, I do like how they all have different carrying packs they use. Not only symbolized by the inventory icon but also shows on the bottom of the inventory as it looks like it is coming out of their choice way of carrying everything.
The puzzles are mostly all fine, and do make you laugh at yourself for not realizing it. Though at some points it does suddenly use logic from video games, but for the most part they do give you some way to figuring it out. Along with this, there are minigames that are tied to the puzzles. With some of the obviously not that enjoyable, the most notable the one connected to the DJ Woo achievement mostly due to how long the replay is and only a few options totally not in the final product. There is also a hacking minigame that I totally see why others do not like it as it can be annoying with limited moves and trying to think in terms of getting pieces from horizontal movement plane to where you need it in the vertical plane, but they do give you bonus tiles to help and you can skip the hacking minigame after one level.
There sort of is a narrator, F1, but it sadly it feels like it is used to explain what happened because they couldn’t think of a way to naturally have it revealed in the story. It is quickly explained to how and why Sandra and Woo was sucked into a game and how he knew about Landon, Larisa, and Cloud messing with it. I do wish what he tells you with his few appearances were naturally put into the game or was found in the real world so you can have more interaction with it. As by the end of the day, they all do not know how it was even possible for real world items to be transferred to a game and I wish they did. It would of been interesting to see Landon researching it or going into the game’s code and seeing that the creator intended for his free game to have a trojan and all the computers with green lights had the game on them. And with them watching Sandra and Woo as well, maybe have Sandra and Woo finding various items that the creator put himself in. And with F1 finding out, maybe have him send vague messages, trying to free up space on the computer to suck them in, and basically doing more than having Landon only doing a hacking minigame. Than show him at the end and hint that he was probably working for someone else like they did.
This way you are actually getting the info by playing through it and going “Huh...this seems suspiciously linked to this event” and “Wow we must be close if he is trying to stop me”.
+ Characters
+ Dialogue
+ Interesting story
+ Little joke about the help center (by pressing F1 in the game)
+/- models can use a little more work in their animations
+/- some sound effects didn’t make sense for some items or was weird
- Wish the narrator/F1 was used less so the information he gives you was naturally revealed to you and the characters
Sandra and Woo in the Cursed Adventure is ultimately for the fans of the webcomic. As I am not familiar with the webcomic, excluding the couple ones I looked at, and how these characters showed their personalities in them, I do feel like I would know them better if I did. Especially with the story pushed by also how all the characters interact, which seems to be unique to how the webcomic does it as well. Though the whole fantasy game scenery does seem like they were also thinking about the people who might not know the pre existing characters. Making this a must play for fans but a maybe for the non fans.

Huge fan of the webcomic. That said, the game was pretty disappointing to me. If you like the webcomic and are always hungry for more like me, then it may be well worth it to go through the game for seeing more of the characters and all that- but they don't quite shine as well here. I finished to the end in anticipation of an interesting story, but the ending felt very abrupt and anticlimatic.
Where to start? The graphics are...okay. The animations were pretty awful. They were very stiff slow and choppy and kept making awkward pauses in the dialogue that really interrupted the flow of the action. The sound effects? My ears were bleeding (especially that one re-used kiss sound effect oh god).
The voice-acting (in English) was all over the place, some of them were okay or pretty good (thankfully Larisa was still pretty awesome) while some sounded like grandpa in a skype call with a $2 mic.
The actual dialogue was pretty amusing. Again, Larisa is best.
The point-&-click stuff was pretty neat, though some parts were a bit too nonsensical/abstract to really solve except hoping to stumble onto it by chance. Then again, I haven't played too much point-and-click, so maybe I'm just really bad at them. I often got stuck trying every combination over and over only to finally realize I overlooked the simplest actions.
The minigames were simple but challenging enough to be fun imo. Plus, the CD's were a nice touch for when they could get too frustrating.
Personally, I would have really enjoyed it if the game's story took place more in the actual setting of the comic and used more of their existing characters that fans would love to see. It would be awesome exploring places that fit into the comic, like the school, cloud's house, the forest, the various places of the city- lots of potential there. Frankly it was hard to feel invested in that medieval setting with its short-lived characters who were little more than walking parodies of a genre.
If they made another game established more firmly in the comic's setting with more of its characters, I'd likely go back for more despite the various technical drawbacks. (please please fix that kiss sound effect though or it'll turn otherwise cute scenes into really cringey moments D:)
So, overall...I feel they could have invested much more time and effort into the quality of the animation and sound. Either that or lower the price to match what was put into it. Definitely room for improvement in the character models but was passable. Would definitely be more appealing with more focus on the comic's setting/characters imo. Good for some laughs and basking in Larisa's firey glory but probably not recommended for people unfamiliar with the webcomic. (then again, I'd recommend them the comic first).

This is an extremely difficult game, with the outcome of battles often feeling very random. There aren't a lot of tactics at your disposal, certainly early on, and so if you start a battle with unlucky unit placement or just have a lot of bad RNG results during the fight then you'll lose pretty much regardless - and that means having your equipment stolen, losing vital days due to injuries, losing character to permadeath - or all of the above.
The setting is nice, and battles can be very satisfying when you don't feel too cheated by chance - but this is definitely a game for those who aren't put off by a steep learning curve and are prepared to invest a lot of painful time learning the ropes.
It's also worth noting I've experienced freezes during loading once or twice which required a restart to fix, and enemy turns can be very slow to process, which can be rather frustrating.

While I wanted to like this game, I cannot help but feel there are some serious underlying issues under the hood.
First off, I would say I am a big fan of games that are difficult. I enjoy a challenge and don't mind if the AI has a leg up on me to compensate. However, unlike X-com or even Darkest Dungeon, this game fundamentally seems to think that introducing arbitrary hardness to every encounter while offering the player very little choice in how to face it is somehow the same as providing a genuine challenge.
First off, there is very little in the way of tactical decision making available to the player once they get on the ground. Despite the AI often having an advantage in unit power, it is usually easy to cheese by bottlenecking a corridor or just massing your units into a single large group that roams the map and turns each battle into a tedious chore of mopping up the stragglers. Given the AI's advantages, what this means is that hoarding your units into a massive group and slowly roaming often guarantees you a victory, while one-on-one fights are usually losses for you (assuming you are fighting with equal units). In theory you are supposed to treat each match as a scramble towards gathering wyrdstones to support the upkeep of your warband, yet you can usually grab enough in your slow trot across the map from the enemy corpses that grab them first. There is simply very little incentive to seperate your units. As such, each match feels tedious and very much like the last.
That said, there is the rare time where the AI may still manage to get the drop on you, and this is entirely due to the aforementioned arbitrary hardness. Like X-COM, you are given a percentage to hit chance that usually seems to border anywhere from 60% to 90%, yet I assure you that you will never hit this much, especially not starting out. Whether it is true that the RNG is genuinely, deliberately stacked against you or not is unknown to me, but I can see why so many people feel that it is.  This persists in to the later stages of the game (I have more playtime than steam is showing) and continues to enforce the notion that the game is deliberately making itself mechanically biased against the player to make up for its shortcomings in AI.
Gradually your units do manage to feel competent and varied, though starting out is quite painful. There is not a ton of variety or customization offered in the appearance of your units which was a bit of a bummer, but its good enough. Yet, I never really felt attached to any of my characters like I did for my X-COM soldiers.
Not much else about the game is particularly noteworthy, good or bad. The graphics feel pretty rough albeit fitting to the universe, and the UI is wonky but not unusuble, unlike what some reviewers have said. The campaign voice acting is nice and the sparse amount of lore building we get is enjoyable for me as a long time Warhammer fan. That said, don't expect there to be any kind of a real "story". The line of sight system definitely could use some big improvements but again, I feel the RNG is the biggest pitfall of this game.
In summation, this game tries to present itself as being a hardcore tactical strategy game, but often comes off feeling like the devs ran out of ideas on how to actually provide a challenge for the player and instead decided to just rig the system to make it 'feel' difficult. The lack of any real strategy outside of hoarding your units or bottlenecking the enemy turns each encounter in to a slog against an obnoxious RNG system that feels like a cover-up for the AI's lack of intelligence. At some point, it stops feeling challenging, fun, or risky, and instead simply becomes a frustrating chore that loses its appeal for the player to continue onwards when they know that there is little in the way of strategical decision making open to them.
All of this said, everything I have seen from the developers seem to imply they are open to feedback (albeit quite unlikely to fundamentally change anything of note at this late in the game's life) and do intereact with the community a lot still, despite the relative age of this game. DLC continues to trickle in and even though some are not fond of the pay model, I don't find the DLC prices all that bad. There does seem to be a small but active community built up around the game, and I imagine multiplayer may relieve some of the game's shortcomings. Still, the bulk of the game is single-player only, so I have to ultimately say I cannot really recommend this game to anyone unless they can overlook the wonkiness of the AI and the short comings of a purely RNG style of gameplay.

For more experienced shmup players, I'd recommend passing on this one, if nothing else, you will propably get bad habits from it.

Compared to many other shmups avaible, the game doesn't bring anything to the table. The stage design, not to mention the extremely simple and dull boss fights is a big turn off, especially the final stage is flat out horribly designed because "It's the last stage, we must make it totally different and stupid", it feels extremely out of place.
Difficulty wise, if you are looking for a challenge, you won't find it until unlocking the "Judgement" difficulty. One of the best shmups on Steam. It has 5 difficulty options and 5 stages. The stages are designed nicely and the bosses are also. Everything looks great and the stages have a lot of details put into them.
The game has a shop system where you can buy ships and challenge levels. The 4 ships you can pick from are all unique. No 2 ships play similar to each other. The challenge stages will also last you a long time. They are difficult objectives to complete in a short section of a stage and there are around 20 of them. You also can't beat the game on Normal difficulty. You need to raise it higher to play the last 2 stages. Leaderboards are included, so you can challenge your friends to the highest scores in the game.
The only thing I don't like about the game, is that there are no upgrades. I always enjoyed upgrading my firepower while playing a shmup, but there is none of that in this game. Jamestown can be completed in around 30 minutes like most shmups, but it has the depth to be played for a lot longer.

In many ways, this is a baby's first bullet hell game.  It's a bullet hell shoot em up that is relatively easy to start, giving you a way to soak up lots of damage and increase your weapons without taking a hit, and it has several different types of ships and weapons for different play styles.  This game's graphics are just gorgeous, from the wonderfully alien martians and monstrous enemies you fight in search of roanoke, to the steam punk ships and bosses.  It's a beautiful amalgam of sprites and pixel art.  What surprised me most is the sound track, honestly.  It's soul stirring in places, particularly the final boss.  I was getting a Final Fantasy 7, Sephiroth vibe of it.  And the difficulty sliders make the game more akin to a true bullet hell the harder you go, so there's something here for all ages, especially with the challenge maps.  Frustratingly, the game only gives you a set number of lives in single player...I wish they gave you one ups based on your score.  That would have made this game perfect.  Otherwise, this is a super fun shmup that anyone can get into.

Many things have been said about Rakuen in these reviews. Some of it I may retread, some of what I have to say may be new.
The first thing I have to say is that I have been following Laura for years on YouTube and other media. Her music has always been extremely powerful and moving, no matter what emotion it was make to invoke. So when she first announced her plans to make a game, I knew that the story was going to drive the emotions home with her powerful compositions. And in that, Rakuen did not fail. All the music, every little bit, is made to evoke something of the story and the environment. The leitmotifs for the big events are all stunning, and squeeze every bit of heart out of the scenes.
Next, I definitely enjoyed the gameplay, even if I got a little confused on where I might have to go or which puzzle to attempt next. The game never slowed down for me, because the pace is like that of a leisurely walk in a park; you enjoy the journey as much as the destination. Obviously, near the end, everything rushes towards the climax, and the emotions become a whirlwind in your mind.
Now, I am warning you, this next passage is going to contain spoilers, so if you do not want to read it, skip to my final paragraph.
All in all, this story had me crying for quite some time. As bittersweet as it is, I would not take back my playthrough for anything. Laura, if you read these reviews, thank you so very much for making this. I continue, to this day, to follow you online, and I always enjoy your work. Rakuen is no different.
I'm not crying, you're just an onion.

I really love this game!
Bought it in sale for only 1 euro, but it's totally worth the 10 euro's.
It's a cute and challenging platformer, which starts easy so you can learn the simple controls and basics, but gets (insanely) difficult pretty soon.
I especialy enjoy playing this with friends in co-op mode, which can be done with up to 8 people. There are multiple ways to play co-op, including racing against each other or shared death, but most of the time we're just trying to help each other get to the end, preferrably with 'the bottle', that unlocks the hard mode version of that level. Those hard levels are really nightmare worthy and I'm very certain that I'll never beat them in my own, if I'll beat them at all. But the normal levels are fun and challenging enough. And there are a lot of them: 5 area's with around 18 levels each (depends on the area). I'm now somewhere in the fourth area, a tropical enviroment, thanks to co-op mode, and after a lot of playing hours, and a lot of deaths, because - warning!- you die A LOT. If you don't like that, don't buy this game.
Another warning, you do NOT have a complete vision of the parcours. Some people will find this annoying - it's inescapable that unexpected spikes will kill you more than once - but I think it adds to the adventure feeling. You never know what will come and when you'll be at the end of a level. A Bob (it's the name of the species, not of the individual meatball-like creature) jumps very floaty, but you can steer in the air and when you land and don't touch any buttons, you'll stand still immediately, not rolling further, like I first expected.
The only big negative thing that I have to mention about this game is that the co-op connection isn't always the best. There have been a few times when we would all get a black screen and it took more than a minute before it would go away and  the level would load, or it would just not load at all. Changing the host helps then. I've also lost connection a few times while playing with a big group, and failed to get back in. I recommend playing this game with one or two other persons.
If you like platformers, this is a must have!
Now go buy this game! ;)
