I like this tiny box, as a general desktop PC extender (screen, audio in/out, keyboard, mouse, via USB or Bluetooth). I use it to some extent for gaming, as the audio experience is leagues beyond what I get at my desk, despite having surround 5.1 systems both there and by the TV, but more time is spent streaming video and audio from browsers and what-not running on the desktop PC. I also use it as a generic remote desktop, having access to all features of Windows remotely. As I have it connected to 1 Gb wired LAN, performance is good. I can't look at Netflix via the Windows app due to DRM issues. I need to use a browser for that, but that works fine. Playing music via Spotify or off-line works great too. There's some lag, so it's probably not optimal for competitive multi-player games. Also, if the PC is already close to croaking on a certain game, you might have to ease up on some of the graphics when playing via Steam Link. At (currently) 90% off it's a steal. At full price it still adds features you didn't have before, and that e.g. Chromecast can't provide. You could use a laptop and Remote Desktop as the same thing, but the Link doesn't take space and is always ready to go. Actually I often sit with my laptop in the TV sofa, while playing a movie via the Link. I bought it at full price.

Charging mindlessly into battle will almost certainly result in death, it only takes one well aimed round to end your life. Enemy soldiers are hard to spot and, unless you remain steady when aiming, almost impossible to hit.
The result is gameplay that surpasses the typical tactical shooter. Every decision has to be made in realtime, often under fire, and with deadly consequences if you make a mistake.
And while the NPC soldiers you fight with can be a bit random, you will miss them when the last man standing is you. Being pursued through a forest at dawn by enemy troops and a helicopter gunship without any backup gets the addrenaline pumping.
Compared to the later versions it looks pretty basic, but it's defintely worth a look.

It was an honor to play this game! It's clear how much love went into every aspect of this game, from the characters to the art to the soundtrack. There is a perfect balance of warmth, humor, eeriness, sadness, hope... there were parts where I laughed out loud, parts where I was legitimately scared, and parts where I cried. Traits of a great story!
The game really builds on itself as you go, reasserting itself until the end when the message is delivered straight to your heart, and it's a message that makes you rethink how you feel about life, makes you want to (at least for me) become a kinder, stronger person.
Nobody embodies the theme of this story better than the character of the Mom. I knew she was going to be awesome and she was indeed my favorite character in the whole game! She's witty, kind, strong, and always there for you. It's so unique in the world of video games that you get to have Mom in your party. There were parts in the game where I was spooked or even downright scared, but the fact that she was with me made me feel surprisingly safe and reassured. A small game with a big heart, that's probably the best way I can describe this game.
tells the story of a hospitalized boy who one day asks his mom to accompany him to the world of his favourite storybook, Rakuen, to ask the Guardian of the Forest for a wish. However, before the Guardian grants his wish, he sets a series of tasks for the boy to complete that revolve around exploring and resolving the different troubles that beset the other patients in the hospital. Thus begins the boy's adventure as he travels between the hospital and the magical world of Rakuen, meets new friends, and faces different challenges, all the while unveiling the patients' stories as well as his own.
While it reminded me of
, I'd say it plays more like the old Zelda games I used to play on my Gameboy Color, such as
. Exploration is tied to your progress throughout the game as you acquire new tools that open up previously locked paths. Puzzles are also present in this game, even if they are not particularly difficult to solve. They are all fairly intuitive and take a trial-and-error approach that never feels cumbersome. Do not however, expect combat, of any kind. While Link may need a sword and shield to do battle in monster-infested Hyrule, the world of Rakuen is quite peaceful and welcoming, and whatever "monsters" you may encounter cannot be defeated with a blade. There is still an inventory as you sometimes need to gather materials to build certain tools or collect special items to complete quests.
The story itself is well-executed and incredibly moving. The game smoothly transitions between worlds to explore the lives of the patients, sometimes as characters in Rakuen, other times as their real-world selves. For instance, the grumpy old man is depicted as a bear in the world of Rakuen, and most of his story is explored there. On the other hand, the story of the little girl, Sue, is initially explored through your interactions with her at the hospital before transitioning to Rakuen as the story progresses. While every one of the patients' stories struck a cord with me, I must admit I really enjoyed Sue's story, mostly because of her interactions with the boy and her wonderful imagination. The game also has a few heart-warming surprises in store that I won't spoil for you.
If I had to critique something however, it would probably be the fact that
spoils the ending very early on. While I admit it was something I had anticipated before playing, I did not think the game would be so blunt about it that early. It moved me to tears right then and there and I still kept playing it so it must have done something right. Also, bear in mind that the closer you get to the end, the more exposition you will see and the less gameplay you will encounter. Lastly, I was a bit taken aback by the scope of the boy's own story, even when there were clues sprinkled throughout the game that hinted at it. I feel however, that his story would have been tighter with a slightly narrower scope.
On a technical side note, the game's resolution is limited to 640x480 due to the engine used (RPG Maker XP). While this never detracted from my enjoyment I put it out there so you're aware. Incidentally, this game is perfectly suited for play on a handheld like the 3DS, and I sincerely hope it comes to the Nintendo Store soon.
The world of Rakuen itself is beautiful to explore, enhanced by the surprising variety of characters and the extensive and rich soundtrack. Seriously, the soundtrack on Bandcamp has 52 tracks, what's over an hour of music, with so many good tracks that it puts quite a lot of AAA game soundtracks to shame. Heck, the game itself puts many AAA titles to shame! For me,
is right up there with games like
,
,
, among others. A lot of love was poured into making this game and it shows many times over.
Ultimately,
is a game I heartily recommend at full price. With a beautiful story that will move you to tears and a world well-worth revisiting,
is one of those rare gems that, sadly, go so often unnoticed. Should you happen to read this review, I pray that will no longer be the case.

This was a game I played hundreds of hours on long before I discovered Steam. As soon as it was available, it was a must-have purchase for me.
Civ IV is a sublime strategy in the truest sense of the word. Spanning over 6000 years of human history, you'll start with a single settler forming a tribal village. Dozens of hours later you could be sending a fleet of warships to control oil deposits in the north pole, taking control of the global market with a corporation monopoly, or ordering a charge of knights in a futile last strike against an Aztec airbase.
It's a game that provides multiple ways to win and even several options to get to each of those conditions. You will compete against up to 18 other nations using diplomacy, warfare, exploration and luck to establish an empire. You will need to stake a claim on finite global resources, defend your borders, make friends and defeat enemies. Spread religion and corporations to control the masses and bankrupt your ememies. Deploy spies to see enemy troop movements or sabotage their reserach and production. Build great wonders to boost your cultural impact. Difficulty is easily scaleable and 'tweakable', providing a fantastic challenge. Perhaps you will triumph...and perhaps you will meet your end at the hands of Mahatma Ghandi's nuclear arsenal. One thing is for sure...you will have many, many replays of this game.
THEN there are the scenarios - various historical or fictional settings that tweak the rules and gives special conditions. See if you can spot the mod (inclided with the game) that inspired their later offering - 'X:COM Enemy Unknown'.
In Short: The greatest strategy game ever made*- there'll be no need for friends, jobs or even sunlight anymore with this baby. The only reason you should not be buying it is because you were reading this review. But it's over now...so go guy it!
*This includes the more recent title 'Civ V' -- a competent game, but inferior in my humble opinion.

Be warned, I'm going to make this wordy. This is something of a braindump based on my time with the game so far.
You might notice a trend amongst the negative reviews of Mordheim having brutal RNG. My first experience with the game was during the free weekend back in August. During the tutorial for learning how to cast spells, my Sister of Sigmar rolled the Mordheim equivalent of a critical failure and died on the spot. That set the tone for the rest of my experience. I went on to watch my initial Skaven Warband get absolutely slaughtered. The whole thing left a sour, RNG-flavoured taste in my mouth and I lost interest.
Fast forward to December and Mordheim hits Humble Monthy. I decided to read some guides and give it another shot. My fresh Skaven Warband proceeded to get rolled, three missions in a row. But something after that clicked for me. The mechanics started to make sense, the random dice rolls behind the scenes didn't seem so one-sided anymore. I was able to guide my plucky rat-men to victory after victory.
At it's core, Mordheim is about embracing failure. Your Warbands and the units within them are disposable. They will die. You'll do everything the 'right' way, only to be punished by a dice roll. Learning to embrace that has been challenging, but has made Mordheim an incredibly enjoyable experience. You learn to make better decisions, to equip your units and train them properly to mitigate these risks. The veteran system also helps get rid of some of the "unfairness", by giving you global perks that make your early game easier with each new Warband. The point is, your skill and planning can and do go a long way towards helping out with the looming threat of RNG.
Given all this, it should be obvious that my recommendation comes with a pretty huge caveat. If everything you've read about RNG and the constant threat of failure sounds like fresh hell, Mordheim probably isn't for you. On the other hand if you enjoy games like XCOM and can handle getting slapped around a little, you might find a shining strategy/RPG gem in Mordheim.

The game is nicely designed and features an original gothical artstyle. The character and enemies look very detailed and well animated. In my opinion, the visuals were crafted with tender, love and care, they positively enhance the atmosphere of the game.
Controls are pretty straightforward; you aim with the mouse and the game offers a tutorial for the moves you are able to do. Also, the Savant - Ascent features complete controller support, for people who want to play that way. Nice!
The soundtrack is what keeps this game alive. The game features a set of electronic/dubstep songs, that accompany you during your play. In my opinion, the music is really awesome and makes the game feel more arcady, even without repeating chiptunes!
Sounds are nice too. Overall, the sound of the game enhances the gameplay and lets you feel the action from start to finish. It really feels like you are playing an arcade game!
The gameplay is kept simple: you, enemies, shooting, surviving. You aim in the general direction enemies are in and shoot. That's it. Disc parts you can find or unlock throughout the game will give you a new track you can listen to, but they also grant you a special power (more damage etc.). There are different powers and all of them make you somewhat stronger. Try to find all of them, in order to beat the endgame content this game has to offer!
Chain up kills to increase your score multiplier and reach that sweet, sweet highscore in the leaderboards. But be careful not to get hit, since it reduces your multiplier, aswell as your lives. Three hits and it is game over for you!
Next to a small story, this game features and endless mode, in which you have to survive as long as possible (and consecutively gain very many points). Lastly, there is a timed mode for the storymode, in which you will need to beat the game as fast as possible. Small eastereggs are also included.
Unfortunatly, music is (as always) a matter of taste. If you feel a strong dislike for said music, I would advise against buying this product.
Be aware of the fact that this game is short and might not keep you engaged for a very long time. Fortunatly, the shortness is compensated with its price. Consider it a tasty snack you discover, so tasty you want to savor it by not eating it too often.
Savant - Ascent is a game that could really be called a new age arcade game.
For a game that small in size and content, I really had lots of fun with it. The soundtrack enhanced my complete experience with it and kept my heart pumping and my head banging. The gameplay feels overly satisfying, wrecking some enemies with POWER OVERWHELMING has never felt that good for me.
So you should definetly give it a try, because Savant - Ascent took the term "Brevity is the soul of wit." and "Sometimes, less is more." very literal. So literal, that I can't even believe I didn't spend more than two dollars on this game.
Friendly advice: Just be careful not to headbang too much or you'll wake up with neck muscle hangover the next day.

Verdict: RECOMMENDED
Before we get into this review, I have at least over 3000+ hours on this game, I have been playing it for 7 years I don't use the Steam version often. Oh and hey to anyone who knows Gonnakillu, Scottyj and my 17 other toons from Argonneson (add me if you do <3)
The actual combat system is definitely one of the best I have used in MMO's I have played my fair share of MMO's and in my opinion the combat system/engine in this game tops all of them, for a game that was released in 2006 (I think) it has a really advanced combat system and I would call it advanced for games today.
To actually have fun with this game you do not even have to have friends playing with you as there is a great group engine which allows everyone around the world to be connected together and play with eachother, you can mark yourself as LFG (Looking For Group). The game is also fun while soloing through quests but you can also have support from hirelings, which is an friendly AI which you purchase to hire for an hour (time doesn't go on whilst not in quests/wildernesses). Speaking of the AI's, although they are sterotyped to be stupid as a pinecone they are actually very useful to have at times and they're very well developed.
For classes/races there are so many options to pick, I think there are a total of 14 classes, but that can change at anytime because Turbine are always updating the game with new classes/races, I also think there is a total of 14 races now that they've added in Gnomes, unforunately I haven't been on to see this yet. The race you pick can also effect your class stability and changes your stats such as Charisma, Wisdom, Strength, for example a Halfling will have decreased Strength and a Drow will have decreased Intelligence, this is also a very good system that stops very over powered builds coming in game.
The servers itself are very good, I do not ever experience lag, whenever I do it is on my end, there are not many maintenances that occur.
The game is F2P but after a certain level lets say, 12 it is very hard to progress without some adventure packs and you will find yourself grinding the same quest a lot, VIP is quite cheap for a monthly subscription, but you can also just buy the adventure packs individually and in your own time. If you are P2P'ing you will have a better time with the game as you will not have to ransack every F2P quest out there as a lot of adventure packs are added frequently that you will have access to once released (as a VIP) You can also either the races/classes or get them for free with VIP, but you can also earn the in-game without implementing a single penny into the game via favor which you earn with every quest you complete, the amount of favor points you get is increased if you do the quest on a higher difficulty (please note there is a lot of F2P classes/races but there is a lot of P2P classes/races as well).
This game can also be used to make a lot of friends which could lead you into a high level guild which makes the whole experience a lot better and more fun. Your guild you have joined or created can also get an airship, you may unlock the first airship at level 20 (guild level) I believe and you will start to unlock better airships gradually when you increase your guild level, these airships can be brought by in game currency (platinum, gold, silver, cooper etc) or Turbine Points. These airships aren't just there for design though, they are able to have buffs on then which increase your stats which are very useful especially when going on high level raids.
The PvP feature is outstanding, I guilty enough, have spent most of my hours in the PvP areas which are normally located in taverns, the most populated one being the Wayward Lobster in Harbor. Although in my server it isn't as populated as it used to be once be (the good ol' days :'( ) it is still a fun feature which you can mess around with friends with, there are also game modes such as capture the flag and all of that shenanigans but I am not sure if it is working shape as I haven't heard of it for a while.
The character creation is an extraodinary engine, it has many options to pick with which can be used ot make a already built build (highly recommended for new players) or a custom build which you can decide where your points go and what spells you decide on. You can even choose your own aliginment (not sure if spelt right) In the past couple of years they've implemented a lot of good features such as new skill trees, epic feats, epic destinies etc and this has changed the game a lot as there is so much more to do. This game, in my opinion, has the best charactor creation engine out there.
If you decide to buy VIP right off the hook make sure you DO NOT start an iconic character straight away as this will take you to level 15 and as a newbie you will be absolutely crushed in quests (that is if you know how to get to quests by that point) make sure you try one of the beginner classes and start off slow and get the drift of the game first, get a character to level 1-15 instead of skipping the levels.
An outstanding feature is True Reincarnation which can be used at level 20 to set you back to level 1 but it will be like you are creating a whole new character as you can pick a whole new race and class but it will be a lot more stronger, powerful and it will give you a lot more options, if you true reincarnate again you will be stronger and more powerful than your 2nd life, after your 3rd life you will have one more boost your points you can add onto your stats etc until it will stay the same and if you do one life on every class you will get a feat that will stick onto you forever called "Completionist" this drasticlly improves your stats etc,  although this will take a lot years to do, I know a few people myself who has done it, I myself have a family member who has done it.
The community in the game is great, but they're also some♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥on there, but hey this is the Internet it is a normal occurance, most of the community are completely chilled and good people and are willing to be your friend have group with you to complete quests together and the community 9/10 helps you out, hey, I had someone give me 100k plat to my brother who was starting out at the time.

I came across this when I couldn't find a decent gaming group near me to play Pen & Paper DnD.
I haven't played it on Steam for a long while (Because technical reasons), but I'm pretty sure my hours played are at least double, if not triple the amount above.
It's not a carbon copy of PnP considering it's made for MMO purposes (I mean, come on, you don't REALLY want to wait six seconds for every single action, do you?) but it's a pretty good representation of it.
A dedicated player can play this game and eventually* access all its content without needing to pay a single penny.
One thing that makes this game stand out from many others out there is its replayability.
Your character isn't capped at its full potential when you reach max level, no.
You can "Reincarnate" characters to make them stronger on recreation, giving them extra perks and bonuses, allowing you to build a better character from level 1 without deleting and re-creating it.
With time, you can go through all the Classes with a single character, no need to create different characters for different classes, though you can still do that, if you so choose.
It's also a rather friendly community overall, so don't hesitate to always ask for help in-game!
*After excessive grinding across multiple servers for currency you can use in the in-game Store.

Challenging platformer which needs a lot of improvements to be as good as other games of this genre. Especially control lags and FOV should be improved.
There is actually a small story behind the game. But to be honest this is not the main part I am buying such a platformer like this or Super Meat Boy, but because of challenging plaform jumping.
The artwork is cute, although it could definitively needs some improvements. Basicly there are three layers. Foreground, main layer where the character is running and the background. Between those layers there seems to be a huge gap which makes it boring to watch at.
It was fun listening to the soundtrack in the first half an hour. Sometimes it was even motivating. Buter after 30 minutes it just got annoying. So I decided to go to the customizing screen and tried to turn the music off, but
. Looks like I have to beat every level on normal in a specific stage to turn the sound for this stage only off.
So all I could do is go to my Windows Sound Settings and disable sound output for the application.
The game is tagged and described as challenging platformer which is just fine. Pretty much it looks like it is inspired from the very good platformer "Super Meat Boy". The challenges in "Bob Was Hungry" mainly consist of jumping into the unknown and maybe you get lucky and pressed the correct controls. This is the main flaw I saw here in this game. If you fail its because you either play the level for the first time and didn't know what will outside the screen or you are playing this level over and over again, but it's just too hard to know where you will land exactly or where the moving spike will be, when you get to the landing spot.
To be able to unlock the hard mode of  specific level you have to do an additional objective. Hidden somewhere in the level there is always a bottle which must be collected. Only if you successfully pick the bottle up and reach the platter (the exit) your time will be saved and the hard mode is unlocked. If you don't collect the bottle you will not be able to beat your own highscore.
Completing a level will reward you with one food item. Collecting the bottle and completing the level will reward you with two food items. Those are picked random, so if you want to complete every level with every food item as a reward you have to play the level over and over again.
What I am missing though is a leaderboard. Of course I can see my own highscore but what is the reason for an highscore if I cannot compare it to the highscore of my friends.
Positive is that there are a huge amount of levels that can be played.
First I was using keyboard controls to play the game because the game did not recognized my gamepad. But replaying today I found the settings where you can calibrate your controler. You even can remap all the buttons to a layout you are very comfortable with.
What I have my difficulties are the lag between pressing a button on the gamepad or keyboard until the character is moving. Especially when you make long jumps into nowhere and have to react very fast because of moving spikes or other evil things.
There are just too many flaws I would like to see to be improved. This is why I cannot recommend it to my friends at this point, but maybe if some things get fixed I will change my review.

Bob was Hungry is one of the most soul crushing games I've ever played. I honestly didn't know it was possible to die 300 times in a game. Bob was Hungry has some great vibrant colours and some areas have some fantastic music (not so much a fan of the space music). The f**king meatballs have eyebrows and blink though, that scares me a little.
Bob was hungry is a platformer on the same caliber of rediculous as super meat boy, the puzzles just get harder and harder until you want to cry yourself to sleep.
Although there is co-op to this game it doesn't exactly add anything except the possibility to have a seperate spawn point instead of back to the start, this leads me to believe that you'd almost be better off never playing single player and going in with a second controller to use as a check point. Because honestly restarting half these levels from the start is a little over the top, especially when you're as bad as me at video games.
The co-op could also do with some of its own levels, giving it a proper co-op feeling; rather than just "lets run through and maybe we'll have fun being stuck together" I'd much prefer a "you step on this button while i step on this one" kinda thing, but alas every pushable button only needed one person.
Hard difficulty made me want to cry when i loaded up the first space level and I don't enjoy sitting there fighting the elements of a game trying to proceed. The fact that the 10% chance you have of really doing anything on some stages is lowered to about a .5% chance and just makes it unbelievable unfun.
I can see how this game would be really addictive to someone who enjoyed this kind of thing, but for me personally it was too much of a challenge and I don't think there'll ever be a time where I'd be able to go back and complete some of the levels I couldn't even get past the spawn.

Don't get me wrong the visuals are still basic, but they are also on point and nicely detailed for the world that Max inhabits. This game has a tremendously old school vibe akin to Heart of Darkness from ages ago. I think people into platformers, and more or less that style of game, will dig this one too. It might turn off some people not quite used to the leisurely pace and childish exterior. The game picks up, though, and before you know it you will be finishing it as the later stages usually have two levels per world. Still, it's a decent 6-10 hour game.
Thematically, it fits in perfectly with a slightly stylized realism that builds itself around somewhat realistic physics. The big draw here is obviously the marker, and you can do a decent variety of things throughout in your quest to save your brother. Drawing vines and branches along with raising rock platforms will be the major concepts in play. The puzzles range from easy to tough and the checkpoints are frequent enough so as to not ♥♥♥♥ you off too much.
MGS and Press Play created a great game here, and it deserves to be played if you have the time. And even if you don't, this game lends itself to extremely short play sessions. There isn't anything out there quite like it so give it a try when you can.

Jamestown is a bullet hell game set in a steam punk world on Mars. If you enjoy bullet hell games then I defintely recommend picking up this game. Everything about Jamestown seems thoughtful. The artwork and music are beautiful. Each level ends with a large and beautifully animated boss. The background art for each level are all unique. As a pixel artist I can tell you that the artwork must have taken ages to put together.
Running through the game on normal will only take a few hours but beating every level on max difficulty will keep you busy for a while (I haven't even unlocked the hardest difficulty level). There are also challenge levels and unlike so many other games it looks like these were thoughtfully put together and not just thrown in as an afterthought.
There is DLC available that adds 3 new vehicles to add to the original 4. This also allows adds the option to spawn as a random vehicle each life.  The DLC is only 2.99 and I'd recommend getthing that as well if you find that you like this game.

So what is Rakuen ?
Well Rakuen is a 2D top down non combative roll playing adventure game with a similar look and feel to the 16 bit super nintendo/sega era ( think of games like the legend of zelda )
This game has a very similar play style.
It's a game by Indie developer Laura Shigihara, who also by the way produces and perfoms some the music and songs in this game which really helps contribute to the telling and the actual feeling of the story.
Now the name Rakuen is a Japanese word which when translated in to English means pleasure garden or paradise, and this is where a lot of the game takes place.
You play as a young boy who wears a cool paper samurai hat and is lying in a hospital bed for some reason, his mother frequently reads the book Rakuen to him.
you learn that Rakuen or the pleasure garden is a wonderful magical land where a mysterious creature lives who is the guardian of the forrest and this guardian has the abilty to grant wishes and if the boy wants to they can visit this place together, the boy states he would like to visit the guardian to make a wish.
Now to help releive the boredom of being cooped up in your hospital bed the doctor allows you to explore the hospital.
As you begin to explore you realise that the hospital has been damaged in some way, the reason for this will become more apparent as the story progresses.
As you continue around the hospital you encounter various patients each with their own individual personality, story and problems.
Their problems touch on some very dark and real world issues such as loneliness Dementia bullying and even death.
this really gives the characters some meaning and depth, it makes you actually care about what happens to them.
Now The patients ask you to do various tasks for them such as retrieving lost items or collecting certain materials or solving basic puzzles, but in order to do this you find youself traveling back and forth to a parallel universe that is connected to reality through mysterious doors that appear, these doors will give you access to the stories fantasy world.
Now When you first arrive in this fantasy world you will be accompanied by your mother, your mother simply helps aid you in the telling of the stroy.
you can speak to her for hints about puzzels or if you just forget your objective, other than that she really serves no other purpose which is a shame as i think there could have been more interaction with one another but thats just a minor gripe.
However she plays a major and poignant and down right emotional role towards the end of the game, So you've been warned.
So You both head off to see the guardian of the forrest and find out that he has been in a deep slumber for some time, in order to wake him and for him to grant you your wish you must first find and collect various songs that tie in with all of the patients you have met, thus creating individual story archs and quest lines for the patients you have met along the way.
the Weird and wonderful creatures that you will encounter in this world are actually some of the patients back in the reality of the hospital, for example an angry bear in the fantasy world who is terrorising a village is actually a grupmy old man named Tony in the hospital, he asks you to help him fix his music box.
This involves you carrying out quests in both worlds and by completing these quests in the fantasty world it has a knock on effect in reality.
By doing this you learn more about their past and hear their stories which brilliantly cross over from the fantasy world in to reality.
This is a very simple format used through out the game, yet it works so well.
Now as you navigate your way through this world  you will notice how happy and bright and colourful and cheerful it is which is a complete contrast to the gloomy monochrome drab look and feel to the hospital.
Giving the world a sense of escapasim from the actual reality.
The artwork of both worlds is really well done from the lovely looking sky islands and bright and vibrant village to the dark and gloomy feel to both the hospital and under ground caves that you have to navigate your way though.
the lack of voice acting in the game is replaced by a text based commentary where you simply have to read the dialog boxes that appears on screen, this in no way detracts from the game but instead it perfectly blends in, now the soundtrack to this game is the real star if pefeclty sets the scenes from joyous occasions to the down right tear inducing moments, i enjoyed it so much that i actually purchased the soundtrack.
Now im sure all this may all sound rather dull and boring to you, as i said at the beginning there is no combat in this game and there are very few ways you can actualy die, as danger is not really a part of the game bar a few timed situations.
but trust me its not dull or boring, its really not.
for this game is a mark of really good story telling it lacks ever so slightly in the begining of the game whilst your trying to figure out everything that is going on, but after a while it really does keep you hooked and your wanting to find out more.
As i said previoulsly it address some very weighty topics as the boy and the patients try to make sense or their cruel reality.
This game really is an emotional roller coaster of a ride so get ready and strap yourself in.
The end scene between the boy and his mother is beautifully well done and is just something you will have to experience for yourself as it tries to point out the message i beleive the game is trying to portray.
That no matter how hard things are, its how we react to them that matters.
The game took me about 8 hours to complete and this can be done faster but there are things to collect that do help prolong the game.
The game costs £6.99 in the UK and is well worth the money but i bought the bundle which includes the sound track for £10.90.
So to finish off this review all i will say is that
I love it when you find a hidden gem like this and you get to simply sit back and play a game that takes you on such a unique and wonderful journy filled with fun and laugher and moments of real sadness that actually make you stop and think about what you do have in your own life.
Now I really dont want this to be a hidden gem I want this to be noticed I want this to played I want the developer to get the credit she deserves as a lot of indie developers kind of get hidden in vast aray of games that are on steam.
So if you can afford it please go out there and buy it and help support the developer.
So Finally Its with high expectaions that i eagerly await the next jounry she takes us all on.

Oh, boy... where do i even start?
This game may be one of the best i've played in the last 2 years. Why? Let's come to that.
"Emotional Rollercoaster" might describe this title pretty well. But, one note here: Not these boring rollercoasters which go up and down. This? This can be compared to those rides where you hang freely, gettting thrown into one loop after another. This game takes your heart and soul and frequently changes between caressing and strangling.
If you liked "To the Moon", you will like this one too. Maybe even better, as i do. But let's get to the facts.
Graphic:
It IS a RPG-Maker Game. Meaning, 640x480 with the option of turning on full screen, pixelated graphics are everywhere. But! It's not as apparent as in other games. There are beautifully drawn pictures of most of the characters who speak and high quality backgrounds. The world itself is crafted very well, unlike other RPG Maker Games it does not feel barren and empty, there are a lots of colours and everything feels like it just needs to be where it is. If you can look over the graphics, you will experience a fantastically written story.
Story:
While i won't spoiler, i have to say it's one of the saddest stories i've experienced in a game. Expect to change between laughing, because of witty and well written humour and crying, because of the events happening to the characters. These themself are, in short, lovable. Even the small side characters may crack a joke which makes you smile.
Gameplay:
Basic. Very basic. You don't fight. You get to run around, talk with a lot of people, investigate events, search every nook and cranny for collectibles and complete a variety of "quests", to progress the story. Occasionally you have a time based escape, which you can fail, but the game autosaves in about every room or area you enter, so it won't be that bad. It's a typical walking simulator, quite similar to "To the Moon". And while i took about 6 hours to complete the game, i'm sure you can do it in 4 or even less. So it's not much, but that is absolutely okay. The story has to end at some point and it does not feel rushed or stretched out. It felt right.
Soundtrack:
Awesome. For a RPG Maker Game? Absolutely outstanding. Not even the actual singing part of Laura Shigihara alone, but also the music in the game itself. It's catchy, it fits the mood of the scene. Very well done.
As you may have deduced: I highly recommend this game if you can forgive the typical RPG Maker graphics. For 9,99€, you can't do anything wrong.

"If you tell me everything will be okay; I'll believe you, you don't have to tell me how."
To The Moon with less outright tearjerking.  Unlike To The Moon, I think Rakuen resonates more with its soul of exploring the relationship between the player character and his mother.  This is lightly touched territory for games, and I'd love to see other games with personal mechanics like Rakuen's "talk to mom" action.
If I had to complain, however, the game is uneven.  None of the puzzles are difficult, but many require stumbling on the solution.  Maps like the hospital or village are richly thought out, but a few other areas feel tacked on.  The story is really five independent plots, and it'd be nice if they were more parallel and interconnected.
In short, absolutely wonderful if you enjoy this sort of game, if not, worth maybe approaching with an open mind.

This game is... very mixed. Despite the fabulous gameplay, beautiful graphics, and seamless combat, it doesn't shine like it should. For a few reasons. If you look at the other reviews on this game, you wil find these reasons repeated by countless others.  None of these would be nearly enough to waver this games progress alone, but all thogether, they pose a serious threat to its sucess. And much of the damage has already been inflicted, with playercount plummeting to ridiculous lows. And here is why:
1: Its obvious that some parts of this game just went unfinished. It really doesnt bother me that much, but I know it gets on some peoples nerves. For example, the colours of your clothing will sometimes change suddenly; or odd geometric shapes will grow out of your player model and flail frustratingly when you move. In addition to this, the new feature of the UI that allows you to convert your excess clothing into fragments (Material used for repairing clothing that was acquired in a damaged state), sometimes just doesnt work, because you cant right click your items (I honestly have no idea why, and im not sure if this problem also exists for console players). Now, all these issues can easily be fixed by quitting to the menu and then going back into the game, but really, a finished game should not have these kinds of problems.
2: Lack of (item) content. Honestly I dont entirely agree. Im not saying that there is a lot of items; to be honest, there really arent that many. But for me, at least, its hard to notice, for 2 reasons. The first is that, in addition to being able to find the same item in different colours/variants, there are lots of hard-to-get items to work towards, and many unique pieces of armor that you can acquire through scavenging or combat. The second is that they keep adding items, so really, im not too worried about it.
3: Lack of (other) content. The map is beautiful and detailed, but small. Im really hoping they add more, and if people keep playing, they absolutely will. The story is... really rather interesting. But its a side note. That said, as a person, I dont look for games with deep fleshed out stories, and so unraveling the mysteries of this game was quite satisfying for me, although I can definitely see why to other people this might be agitating. Also, after a while it gets tedious fighting the same enemies over and over, but if people stick with this game, they are sure to add more of those too.
4: Buggy. The game crashes. It can be quite annoying. There arent very many gameplay bugs, aside from the ones I already mentioned about clothing and the UI, but still. Some crashing is inevitable, but Absolver's really should have been minimalized to a greater extent by this point.
Honestly thats about all I cant think of.
Now let me tell you what I love about this game.
-Its fun, very very fun.
-It's difficult, rewarding, and exciting
-Everything is balanced, and this is done well, without the problems some other games have of buffing/nerfing unbalanced aspects to oblivion
-Its fast paced, and intuitive
-The art is fabulous, and the map is really quite cool
-The game rewards both offline and online play, so if you dont feel like fighting a pvp match, you can still have fun.
-This games fighting system is innovative, and absolutely astounding when compaired to other fighting games. It allows for FULL custimisation. You can build a deck up from nothing, exactly the way you want it, and fight with a style that is uniquely your own. And if you find you cant seem to make one that works, or you just arent privy to putting in the time it takes to perfect this, you can join a school and gain a combat deck created by someone else; which you are able to use immediately, whether or not you know all the moves in the deck.
-Although this game does lack some content, the content it has is fabulous.
All in all, although there are issues, I really do encourage people to play this game. For me, this game was more than worth the 30$ price tag. It has the potential to be a real gem, and is already a good game as is. All it needs is a little bit of love, and for players who see its value to keep putting their trust into this potiential. Give Absolver a fighting chance, and Im sure it will blow you away.

Ahhh, Vagante.  It’s like the pixelated version of the Dark Souls’ franchise you wish you could play on a potato powered by combustible lemons but couldn’t because A) you had no potatoes that had a 1920x1080 LCD screen, and B) you had no combustible lemons because those were outlawed after Aperture Science used them to burn your house down.  …With the lemons.  Now that I’ve got your attention, my review will follow.
[GRAPHICS/ART STYLE]
The graphics portion of Vagante is more like a lifestyle choice when someone says they’re Demisexual.  They’re not bad by any means but the game has its own flair and spark to it through the quirky pixelated art.  Every dungeon, though dark, bleak, grey, sad, and full of everything that wants to have you murdered so their children can live another day to avoid being grave robbed or psycho mass-murdered, it has a dilapidated feel to it, like other dungeon crawlers before you were killed there and you want to just loot their dead bodies for the stuff they were carrying.  The sprites are interesting and remind me something of Terraria in their forms.  It has a gothic, playfully serious tone to it and looks like an adventure waiting to happen.
[GAMEPLAY]
Gameplay is addicting, fun, and the “just one more time” kind of vibe to it.  I will say though, that the remapping the controls to your liking helps EXTREMELY unless you’re used to using the D-pad to move around instead of using the left thumbstick.  The in-game text involving button use is literally “button 1, 2, 3, 4” etc. and isn’t labeled as “Press X, A, B, Y,” etc. instead.  It’s not that big of a deal but it is a little frustrating when you don’t remember which button you assigned as “button 4”.
There are shops located around each dungeon area in which you can buy things from using the coins you just pawned off some dead creature just trying to feed its family in a run-down community home you just sacked.  You can choose to buy things or not to buy them.  Additionally, you can do neither of those things and instead kill the shopkeeper and steal all his gear.  Depending on how skilled you are at not getting crushed by surprise boulders, getting shanked by a bunch of spikes or even killed by dragons, flying eyeballs, arrows, and drowning, you can kill him.  Did I mention you will likely get killed by a boulder?
The leveling up system in Vagante is more akin to your traditional level-up system in any normal RPG.  You have Strength, Intelligence, etc. but also perks you can pick.  So it’s akin somewhat to Fallout 4’s level-up system and it’s pretty damn cool.  There’s not too much to say about it other than
[SOUND DESIGN/MUSIC]
I normally do not review particular sounds or music in games.  But as plain as Vagante is, it has a very fantasy like vibe.  It’s not epic (lookin at you, Skyrim), it’s not really a fruity fantasy thing (here’s looking at you, Oblivion!), but it is—as I said—very gothic but not brooding.  It’s an adventure.  But all the sounds and the plain music (if I recall, there is some music) all make for a wonderful atmosphere.  You spend more time concentrating on not getting crushed to death by boulders and killed by the 3rd son of the slime you murdered eight dungeons ago, but the sounds are nice to listen to.
So here’s the rundown.
Pros:
+ Art style is brilliant, dark, and different
+ Gameplay is addicting
+ Combat is plain but it helps keep you on your toes and doesn’t require a lot of thinking or planning
+ gear is not hard to come by
Cons:
- buttons not labeled as on controller (not that big of a deal though)
- Game likes to hang up a little here and there but since its early access it’s forgivable
- boulders have a higher K/D ratio than you will after two dungeon runs
10/10 would get constantly killed by boulders again

Atmosphere, music, gameplay and replayability are all hitting top tier for me with this game. There is enough randomness to keep me coming back to what i can only describe as an artistic rendition of a smash-your-face-into-a-brick-wall sim. Several classic styled equips and items from similarly styled older games exist within an extremely challenging package. As with most of these types of games, there are the standard strategies involved in progression and there are rewards for grinding through countless deaths.
What sets this apart other than what i consider perfectly executed atmospheric stylizations, is the fact that at no point is that great item going to make you beat the game, only make it slightly less ridiculous. And there is almost no guarantee that you will find anything useable to your current build causing you to change tactics and approach on the fly. There is enough regularity to create a foundation of approach, but enough randomness to encourage a variety of newly invented curse words to project at your screen.
TLDR: buy it

Too many blind drops/jumps and obscured insta-kills for my taste. Some levels are nigh-impossible to complete on the first go without dying because you simply can't see the spikes until a nano-second before you land on them. That's what makes Super Meat Boy so great. It's 100% fair. If you die, it's because YOU messed up. Not because you couldn't see the spikes until you landed on them. There are several instances in this game of Bob getting hidden behind a tree or the camera angles hides him behind a wall... That you're trying to climb... And then when you finally emerge from behind the tree or wall, surprise! Spikes! Much of this could be avoided simply by zooming out the camera a little more. Not all of it, obviously, but maybe 85-90% which would be a huge deal.
Bob Was Hungry doesn't get it all wrong though. Not at all. The speed is perfect and the controls are pretty tight. (Not perfect but certainly above average and good enough that they feel comfortable and you don't feel like you're fighting the controls rather than the levels.) The level design suffers a little from lack of flow so you have to stop and wait all the time — i.e. it doesn't feel like it was designed for speed (and neither does the mandatory condiment bottle which could go to hell for all I care) but overall it's very decent. I would argue that it still needs some work but the foundation is really good.
I wish I could leave the review neutral because I would certainly recommend the game if a few of the biggest kinks get worked out, but in its current state I can't in good conscience recommend it to any platforming enthusiast.

Okay, so I'll be the first to admit that this is not the MMO for everyone. It is rather dated, has a few issues once in a while, and lacks some of the quality of life features of some newer MMO's. However, it is a character builder's dream, with the ability to endlessly tinker with various builds and classes and the freedom to build your character however you want, with stats, skills, and feats freely allocated allowing for clever and unique builds for those who want to try something new and impressive optimization for power gamers. The community is by and large decent, and while there are probably a few bad apples, I haven't had any terrible experiences. The game is both solo and party friendly, and the more recalcitrant solo players can bring along hirelings, AI companions, to help out if the going gets tough. Dungeons can be run on four difficulties, a pansy mode for cowardly weaklings, a normal mode for weaklings, a hard mode for regular players, and expert for power builds! (Okay, I generalized there.) There is a lot of content for free, and subscribing unlocks access to most of the content for a monthly fee. Otherwise, you can buy or earn turbine points to get content packs to expand your experience. The cash shop is prevalent and offers advantages, but free to play is sufficient to get a good start in the game and there's not really a crippling disadvantage to free players that would force them to pay.

Bob was Hungry is a difficult precision platformer which emphasises on a somewhat of a trial-and-error playstyle. The game seems very similar (if not almost identical) to the hit game "Super Meat Boy!" - With the exception that it is a different art-style, and of course 3D.
The game is incredibly challenging - I have been a platformer for years and was surprised to see some of the early levels be so difficult. However, after one or two failed attempts you can easily do the level. Some of the obstacles placed are in ways that you may not notice until you either land right next to it, or right into it - Highlighting the trial-and-error playstyle I mentioned.
Despite it's difficulty, the game is incredibly forgiving. There is no life system, no punishment for dying and no setting you back - Instead you have a death counter in the top right, tracking how many times you died attempting that level. The death counter will stick on your personal best (If, of course, it was your personal best attempt) and will go down with further attempts.
Each level has a secret "sauce" that must be found to complement the main dish at the end of the level. It isn't needed to complete it, but it adds an extra reason to explore levels and take more risks if you're a completionist.
I would recommend this to seasoned platformers and to people who are looking for a humourous yet challenging game.

Bob Was Hungry is a difficult 2.5d platformer along the same vein of Super Meat Boy's wall physics and IWBTG's obstacles. Bob will roll around, avoiding spikes and other nonsense in his never-ending quest to eat all kinds of odd combinations of food.
I have played through the normal mode, and the difficulty curve of the game is well designed. It teaches basic mechanics, the progressively gets harder as you hop from world to world. Eventually, the game will out-right try to kill you at every possible jump. A real challenge for all skill levels!
I highly recommend this game. I have played (and continue to play) a multitude of difficult 2d platformer games (SMB, Dustforce, IWBTG and its fangames, etc.) and this one has truly found a place amongst them.

Fortress Forever is a free Source mod version of Team Fortress meant to update and refine the
/TF Quakeworld experience for the present day. It has a nice nostalgic feel and fast-paced gameplay, but unfortunately also a very tiny community - a serious problem for any competitive multiplayer game.
While ostensibly geared towards multiple playstyles à la
and managing to provide a similar diversity of class gameplay, in practice the game is more balanced around the movement techniques of concussion grenade jumping and bunny hopping, meaning veterans who have mastered these skills will almost always have a definite advantage over newer or less dexterous players.
These skills also usually require more dexterousness and skill to even pick up than TF2's equivalent Scout movement and explosive jumping. Expect to see FF Scouts and Medics literally zooming in and out of your base with your team's flag, dropping grenades at your Engineer's sentry nest to boot. (Also, grenade spam is still annoying. It's even harder to detect grenades than in TFC due to the game's speed, and on top of that you're still able to time throws for maximum surprise.)
What's alternatively neat and concerning is that concjumping and bhopping were emergent: they weren't intended by the developers of TFC, but arose out of the game engine's quirks due to its similarity to Quake's engine and its movement tricks, which the original Team Fortress mod used. FF on the other hand makes them central game mechanics to appeal to a niche of die-hards who were dissatisfied by TF2, for better
worse.
There's still a solid game here, don't get me wrong. It's not bad, it's just more of an offshoot of Team Fortress than an evolution. For the average TF2 player I'd recommend this more as a piece of history, and as an entertaining diversion with friends. The community just isn't there to support a better game experience on par with the rest of the Team Fortress series, and most of what
there will probably run rings around you. Compare to Team Fortress Classic, which despite serving as the conceptual base for FF has a less demanding skill floor and a small yet serviceable community that hangs around to this day.

If I am not mistaken, this might very well be the first review I have ever written... and this story deserves it! I was skeptical at first, as I hadn't really ever played any text-based adventures (odd, since i I am an aspiring author), but this little epic left me pleasantly surprised. I remained enthralled for hours, enjoying every moment of this steampunk world with its unique yet familiar historical elements, and characters you could really feel like you have gotten to know. The only issue I had was the end. NO, not the ENDING, which was as masterfully constructed as the rest of the story, I mean the fact that, like any story, it had to come to an end. I could have easily spent hours, if not DAYS more with this story. I can honestly say that A Study in Steampunk may have just given me a new obsession with text-based adventures.

A Study in Steampunk: Choice by Gaslight delivers on its claim to cmnbine classic elements of Gaslight literature into something new, but still familiar. The story of the former battlefield surgeon who works for the goverment of a technology-based society which struggles with a magic using enemy is shaped by the choices you make.
The game often gives your the freedom to define the motivation of your character, asks you why to story progessed in certain directions and gives you choices that not only are quite different, but sometimes make the decision which path to follow quite tough. So it creates tension even if all you have to do is clicking a button.
It's well written in an gracceful style that fits the theme of Steampunk. The action scenes are quick and suspenseful, the game gives you more ways to handle them then just firing a gun. The romance scenes - at least the gay one I played - were  neat, sweet and well crafted. I actually was invested in the ups and downs of that part of the story, because the game doesn't shy away from the fact that in this fictional victorian-based era this kind of love had to be a secret one. That strengthened my ambition to find a way for a happy ending.
At the end the story worked for me and gave me goosebumps in its final chapter when all my character did and did not had a share on the outcome of the story.
One minor flaw is that theere is no recap after a finished chapter like in other Choice by- or Choice of- games. I'd have like that as a reminder of what went well and what went wrong during my time I played the heroic ex-battlefield surgeon.

Of all the "Choice of" games I've played this one has to be my favorite. While it draws inspiration from classic tales, it succesfully weaves in creative and original storylines that keep you hooked. I usually just do a single playthrough of a game and go back to quickly change my choices and skim through the different outcomes, but I actually felt compelled to take my time and enjoyed replaying Choice by Gaslight. The characters feel real and their personalities and views make them enjoyable to interact with. They're people and have certain opinions set in stone, but they aren't as prone to flipping out on you if you do one thing wrong like a lot of the other games seem to do. The author was thoughtful enough to give you a whole list of dialogue options to choose from so you don't feel as penciled in or as forced into a strong opinion when you mean to be moderate like many other Choice Of games often do. The characters and story as easy to get invested in and fall in love with (i don't want to admit how many times i've replayed this to re-romance one character *cough* Alexandra *cough*) and the game gives you many chances to develop your MC. It also, thankfully, has opportunities to save your progress as the end of each act. It's a shame that they gender-lock your MC and have no character relationship meter like some other Choice Of games have, but I can't recommend this game enough and only pray that there's hopefully a sequel for it someday.

400 hours of Civ IV later, I can still recommend this to you, I have not gone insane. It's a classic turn-based empire game with real charm, character and a grammy winning theme song. But, and this but is a Nicki Minaj scale but, turn the turn speed up to quick, set the world size to small, with random terrain generation and a full house of 16 civs, and watch your hour-or-so long chaotic power struggle ensue.
Of course, if you were looking for a more epic game, the RevDCM mod pack alongside one of the larger scale earth maps, or a huge scale random map, will set you up for one of the most enjoyable empire building sim game experiences you can get.
To round up, a flexible game with stunning audio, that can be tailored and played to pretty much anyone's needs. A great game and worth picking up.

(BTW, if you're wondering why my in game time is short, its because I played the Wii release first, back in 2011-ish)
This game is a disapointment. It promised to bring the franchise back to its roots, but it failed.
I'm not saying this game is horrible, it just doesn't feel like a traditional (classic) Sonic title.
Issues with the game:
- The level designs feel way too linear -
There are way too many large bottomless pits in stages, boostpads that make you go fast, springs that lead to eachother. It almost makes the game feel like an autoscroller at some points. Many of the level's designs are completely uninspired, they're basically rehashed from the first 2 Sonic Games.

- Splash Hill Zone is your average Green Hill Zone-ish level. This Stage's boss is based off of Green Hill's.
- Casino Street Zone is basically Casino Night Zone. It almost feels like a carbon copy of the zone from Sonic 2 at some points. Again, this Stage's boss is based off the one seen in Casino Night.
- Lost Labyrinth is a Labyrinth Zone-ish stage. Nothing much to say here, many of the features from Labyrinth Zone are present here. This stage's boss is based off the one featured in Labyrinth Zone. Noticing a pattern?
- Mad Gear is basically what would happen if Scrap Yard Zone and Metropolis Zone had a baby, as it feels like both of their level designs have been combined together. Not that its a bad thing. The boss here is based off of Metropolis' boss.
- E.G.G Station is the final stage in the game. It consists of a boss gauntlet, and then the big bad, recycled straight from Sonic 2. The final boss is Sonic 2's final boss.
The only thing that makes these bosses different, is that after the fourth hit, they turn into a more powerful version of the original boss. For example, Splash Hill's boss starts flinging the ball towards you.
I was rather disapointed to see that there where no new level themes for Sonic 4: Episode 1. Like, come on Sega, you're calling THIS a sequel to Sonic 3 and Knuckles?
I'll give it that this was only Episode 1, but even Sonic 3 had more level content than this, and that game contained only half of what was planned.
- The Graphics -
Now, this complaint only applies to the PC version. (No, this isn't about Sega not choosing Sonic's classic design).
Sonic's model looks way too shiny. I think this issue is a PC exclusive one though, I don't remember it being as shiny when I played the WiiWare release, though I'll have to check that later.
- The Music -
Pretty mediocre, especially the soundfont. I know this has been said to death before, but it sounds like a bunch of cats.
None of the melodies really stuck to me, it just felt way too generic and unoriginal.
- Stuff I can get behind -
That aside, just because most of the content in this game is unoriginal, or has been used in previous games doesn't mean this game isn't fun to play.
If you don't consider it a sequel to Sonic 3 and Knuckles, its a decent (modern) Sonic game by itself. While the physics don't match those of the genesis games, they're by no means bad.
While the level design can get tedious at times, it's still enjoyable. Not the best, but it could be worse.
If you just want a game to play casually, or are just bored, then Sonic 4: Episode 1 is probably a good choice. Otherwise, just play something else.
If you want to pretend this game never happended, Sonic Retro has tons of rom hacks and fan games that could easily be considered better then this, so check that site out if you want to.

Empire is definitely one of my favourite titles in the Total War series but for a lot of TW gamers I talk to they don't often understand why. Empire ranks fairly low in terms of reception alongside other contemporary titles despite being the only TW game set in the Georgian era. I'm going to avoid doing a huge broad review of the game, and instead focus on two points I'd like to raise for the new player:
1) The battle engine
This gets a lot of hate right off the bat. Essentially, before Empire if you charged two units of infantry together in any preceding game they would smush into a realistic mass and start going to town on one another. If four of your guys surrounded one of the enemy, they would all attack together and punch his lights out. Since the Warscape engine was introduced with Empire, the combat is reduced to kill moves only. This means that only one soldier can kill any one other soldier at any one time, and it is based on pre-scripted and often quite lengthy kill moves. Combine this with a very badly-designed unit collision system? If you look at a melee battle, it's like watching Cheerios with ADHD fight for control of the milk.
Empire does reduce this impact somewhat. With the basis being on firelock warfare above everything else, the vast majority of your battles on this game are going to be conducted at range with the major exception of cavalry charges. The engine is nowhere near as prominent in this scenario, and I actually think the musket volleys look great when they pick out six or seven blokes from across the enemy's front line. I cannot excuse the melee though, it just looks awful.
2) Campaign Diplomacy
The campaign itself was a lot of fun for me. I found the politics system a little dry and underused, but aside from the occasional spot of lag the campaign map was by and large really enjoyable. I have played a Swedish and Prussian game recently and really enjoyed both aside from one thing: the diplomacy.
The diplomacy makes no sense. The AI factions ask for backwater regions all the time, they refuse alliances and trade agreements for no good reason, the factors influencing international reputation are incredibly difficult to manipulate and almost impossible to move back to positive/negative after they have gone too far in either direction and above all it just lacks any kind of logic and breaks the immersion.
There are tons more pros and cons to the game, but I felt I'd keep my review nice and concise and focus on the two biggest deal breakers for me. Even with those in full effect, I still love this game and have great fun both on single and multiplayer. I'd recommend it for sure!

I had my doubts when I bought this but couldn't resist the 5€ price tag. And overall I can't say that I am dissapointed. Connection works fine on wired network using Asus RT-N66U router and I haven't noticed any serious lagging or stutters. I wanted to be able to play games and watch movies from my pc in the living room and a long Hdmi cable would have been a bit inconvienient as I would have to connect the controllers to the pc in the other room.
Some pros and cons here:
+Works as it should
+Works like a remote desktop also so you can use windows and play other than Steam games with it too.
+Xbox 360 controller can be used to control desktop so you don't necessarily need keyboard and mouse
+In addition to the above, X360 controller works as a mouse/keyboard hybrid in games that doesn't support controller (nice for slower point and click games).
-When I boot the device from the controller the controller needs to be unplugged and plugged again or the link doens't take any input from it. No big deal but annoying.
-Occasional freezing. (really rare)

I would recommend the Steam Link with a very important caveat: hardwire it! I have mine set up via powerline adapters and so far it has been great. I've heard (though not tried) that the wireless mode is less than optimal. I feel like it is a niche product that only people with certain setups will actually get use from; i happen to be one of these people for the following reasons:
-I like couch co-op games
-My monitor is too small  for four people to crowd around
-My living room TV is better suited for this
-I have powerline adapters that keep the connection hardwired
-I already have a host of wireless Xbox 360 controllers
Honestly, if most of the above doesn't apply to you, I'd skip this product. If it does, then I'd give it a huge thumbs up!
One last note (something I had trouble finding out about this product before purchasing): I use a Zettaguard Xbox 360 Wireless Adapter and it couldn't be easier! I just plugged the adapter into the Steam Link and voila! My controllers synced perfectly. I was worried because it wasn't listed as "officially supported" but it worked out just fine.

Call of Duty®: Advanced Warfare, developed by Sledgehammer Games (co-developers of Call of Duty®: Modern Warfare® 3), harnesses the first three-year, all next-gen development cycle in franchise history. Call of Duty®: Advanced Warfare envisions a powerful future, where both technology and tactics have evolved to usher in a new era of combat for the franchise. Delivering a stunning performance, Academy Award® winning actor Kevin Spacey stars as Jonathan Irons - one of the most powerful men in the world - shaping this chilling vision of the future of war.
All digital purchases of Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare include the bonus Digital Edition Personalization Pack with a custom weapon camo, reticle set and playercard.
Power Changes Everything.
An Advanced World
Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare takes place in a plausible future in which technological progress and today’s military practices have converged with powerful consequences.
In this carefully researched and crafted vision, Private Military Corporations (PMCs) have become the dominant armed forces for countless nations outsourcing their military needs, redrawing borders and rewriting the rules of war.
And Jonathan Irons, the founder and president of the world’s largest PMC - Atlas Corporation - is at the center of it all.
An Advanced Soldier
Powerful exoskeletons evolve every aspect of a soldier’s battle readiness, enabling combatants to deploy with an advanced lethality and eliminating the need for specialization.
The introduction of this gameplay mechanic delivers enhanced player movement and verticality through boost jumps and grappling, covert cloaking abilities, and biomechanics that provide unparalleled strength, awareness, endurance, and speed.
With the advent of the exoskeleton and newly advanced armor and weaponry, every soldier commands tactical freedom in any terrain unlike ever before, fundamentally changing the way gamers play Call of Duty across all modes.
An Advanced Arsenal
Harnessing the power of next-gen platforms, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare introduces a new hi-tech, advanced arsenal and ability set, arming players with all-new equipment, technology, perks, and vehicles like hoverbikes and highly specialized drones.
Players can also choose between standard ammunition and an all-new class of directed-energy weaponry that enables totally new gameplay dynamics.
And with exoskeletons delivering a massive force multiplier and unprecedented tactical freedom, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare evolves every firefight.

Max: The Curse of Brotherhood has been a pleasing experience on the eyes. I got sick over the weekend and wanted something childish to entertain myself. And this game has "children game" screaming all over it.
That being said, it reminded me of the days when I was young, and we were stuck infront of the TV trying to solve donkey kong levels and crash bandicoots. This game is like a mixture of those old games and Trine where you need to "draw" things to help solve the different levels.
I was a little intimidated by having to jump around and draw at the same time, however any moment where you're in action. (Like running from a giant child-eating monster) and have to draw a rope, or a bridge, or something the time slows down. It's still challenging enough that I mess up and die a few times, but easy enough that I could easily see this being one of the first games a child tries to play.
I had quite a few good laughs on Max's behalf, his animations were lovely. You could crawl through narrow spaces, but if you didn't do it soon enough you'd hit Max's big head. I giggled. Several times. As Max hit his head, fell down, got stuff thrown ontop of him as he moaned, complained and cried.
Pick this up on the next sale! It's worth the few hours :) Only a pity the developing company got bought by another company that isn't focusing on PC games. I'd love to see more stuff from these guys!

After about 8 hours of playing, here are my thoughts...
1. This game is much more polished than TFC because TFC uses an older engine.
2. The people tend to be more well behaved the people you see on pub TF2 matches.
3. The game is more balanced than TF2 and has a faster pace.
4. There are no teleporters in FF, meaning that the Engineer class is almost exclusively for defending the flag.
5. You get only the stock weapons and no hats.
Conclusion: FF is a good, free alternative to TFC and has a much faster pace than TF2. This is offset by the lack of players. However, when you do find a server, with people playing, it is very fun and very much worth your time.
I hope this review was helpful to anyone considering whether they should play FF or not, and if you do like FF, I hope to see you in a game. Have fun and Happy Fragging.

This would be an awesome game even if you had to pay money for it. The fact that it's free blows my mind. It's perhaps even a disservice to the game, as many people will assume that you get what you pay for. This game is so much more. The writing, story construction and characterisation easily rival games I've bought for $20 or more.
My favorite bits:
. The main character is not a bland & boring milquetoast or a pure-as-snow waif who bravely endures her traumatic past. She has a traumatic past. And it's made her the nastiest piece of work this side of a Grim fairytale. Cinderella? Riiiight, she'd give the evil step-sisters a run for their money. But her characterisation makes perfect sense, and her starting point gives her huge possibilities for growth and a character arc.
. Though sometimes random, it seems to me many of the choices are not "choose what will please your romance option" to get the good reaction, it's "choose what makes sense for the main character to say at this juncture" even if it's rude, or cruel, or aggressive. Which is a lot more satisfying and logical. Also, often more fun :)
. Characterisation for both heroes and most of the villains is well thought out and detailed. There are no black-and-white characters here, just people who make mistakes. The difference is that the good guys try to fix things, the bad guys double down.
. Once you get past the prologue and chapter 1 (and a good adaptive save system means you don't need to redo those, or you can skip them easily), each story is very different. You do NOT feel like you're reading the same book 5 times with slight variations. Each of the 5 paths concentrate on one or two other side characters to allow them to develop further. You really do have to play all the paths to get the full flavor of the story. More to the point, you'll really want to.
My only quibbles is that some of the choices really do seem a bit random. Also, they do not impact the story. This is not a story where your choices will influence the end game in any significant way. There are a few key choices, usually near the end and easily reversed if you've saved, that will shunt you into a Bad Ending, but other than that, most of them are for flavor or to underline how the main character has evolved.  This is not really a quibble, since that's just the kind of game it is, but it's good to be aware of.

Here are some brief reviews on the routes. I'll try not to spoil
: Rod's route was first for me. I was actually pleased with how the story handled the step-siblings trope. It didn't come off too heavy handed and I kinda enjoyed Lucette and Rod gradually learning to tolerate each other. Still, I didn't feel invested in their relationship that much. : I was surprised at how much I liked him. Usually I'm not a fan of the "vain" type of characters, but Karma came off mysterious and humorous enough for me to stay invested in his story. I'm glad I did, because his route is actually where I started to tear up in certain moments. I was more emotionally invested in Karma than Rod, but still not "sold" as my number one route. It was nice to see Lucette more involved and show more initiative in this route, though.
: yeah...skipped him for now. I'll do his soon...sorry
: ....Why you do dis, Dicesuki? In all seriousness, if you want to cry ugly tears, play this route. In all the previous routes, Fritz goes "missing". You'll finally be able to find out what happened and how your loyal knight is involved in the plot. This one is by far the most heart-wrenching, but still utterly sweet. Both Fritz's and Waltz's route were beautifully written, but if I had to compare them...this one wins in feeling empathetic with a character. I feel like the further down we go, the more emotional I get. Fritz's route sheds a ton more light on the world of Angielle, as well as the other side-characters in the game. Prepare the tissues, folks.
: Although Dicesuki remains silent on their FAQ page, I consider this the "canon" route. Where to begin...I fell in love with Waltz way before I got to his route, and when I finally got there...I don't think I can go back. Waltz's story is incredibly endearing, but I'm struggling on how to describe it without spoiling. I think Lucette shows the most character development in this route and I found myself eagerly cheering her on through my tears lol.
